Legacy API key authentication is **deprecated** (removal planned for v3) — see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`. 21: 22: ### Request format 23: 24: `Content-Type: application/json` is required for all `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` requests. 25: 26: ### Response envelope 27: 28: Every response is wrapped in a standard envelope: 29: 30: ```json 31: { 32: "success": true, 33: "data": {}, 34: "error": null, 35: "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" } 36: } 37: ``` 38: 39: On failure, `success` is `false`, `data` is `null`, and `error` is an object: `{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} }`. Validation failures (`400`) include a field-level `errors` array. Server errors (`500`) include a `request_id` in `meta` — include it when contacting support. 40: 41: ### Error codes 42: 43: | HTTP code | Meaning | 44: |---|---| 45: | `400` | Bad request — validation failed; body contains field-specific messages | 46: | `401` | Not authenticated | 47: | `403` | Forbidden — authenticated but not authorized | 48: | `404` | Not found | 49: | `409` | Conflict (e.g., duplicate dataset name) | 50: | `422` | Unprocessable entity — business rule violation | 51: | `429` | Rate limited | 52: | `500` | Server error | 53: 54: ### Rate limits 55: 56: Requests are counted in three categories: **standard**, **bulk**, and **sync**. Every response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp) headers; on `429`, wait until the reset time before retrying. 749: 750: ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 751: 752: ### Webhook signature verification 753: 754: When a webhook is created **with a `secret`**, every delivery includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header containing the **HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body**, keyed with that secret. Verify it before processing any delivery: 755: 756: 1. **Read the raw request body** — the exact bytes as received. 1: # Developer Notes - DataSync API
2: # These are internal notes from the dev team - NOT for external publication
3: # Last updated by multiple contributors
4: 
5: == AUTH STUFF ==
6: We use JWT tokens now. Changed from API keys last sprint (v2.1).
7: Token expires in 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
8: Header format: Authorization: Bearer <token>
9: Login endpoint: POST /auth/login - takes email+password, returns tokens
10: Refresh: POST /auth/refresh - takes refresh_token in body
11: 
12: BUG: Sometimes 401 returns instead of 403 when token valid but perms wrong
13: TODO: Fix in next sprint (JIRA-4521)
14: 
15: == DATA ENDPOINTS ==
16: 
17: /datasets - GET list all datasets for user
18: params: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100), status (active|archived|all)
19: returns array of dataset objects
20: 
21: /datasets/{id} - GET single dataset
22: 404 if not found or not owned by user
23: 
24: /datasets - POST create new dataset
25: body: { name: string (required, 3-100 chars), description: string (optional), tags: array }
26: returns created dataset with id
27: 
28: /datasets/{id} - PUT update dataset
29: same body as POST but all fields optional
30: returns updated dataset
31: 
32: /datasets/{id} - DELETE soft delete (sets archived flag)
33: returns 204 no content
34: 
35: /datasets/{id}/records - GET records in dataset
36: pagination same as /datasets list
37: params: sort (field name), order (asc|desc), filter (JSON encoded query)
38: 
39: /datasets/{id}/records - POST add record(s)
40: body can be single object or array for bulk insert
41: max 1000 records per request
42: 
43: /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} - PATCH update single record
44: body: partial record object
45: 
46: /datasets/{id}/sync - POST trigger sync with external source
47: body: { source_id: string, mode: "full"|"incremental" }
48: returns job_id for async tracking
49: 
50: /jobs/{job_id} - GET check job status
51: response: { status: "pending"|"running"|"completed"|"failed", progress: 0-100, error: string|null }
52: 
53: == ERROR CODES ==
54: 
55: 400 - bad request (validation failed) - body has "errors" array with field-specific messages
56: 401 - not authenticated
57: 403 - forbidden (authenticated but not authorized)
58: 404 - not found
59: 409 - conflict (e.g., duplicate name)
60: 422 - unprocessable entity (business rule violation)
61: 429 - rate limited (100 req/min for free tier, 1000 for pro)
62: 500 - server error (we log these, include request_id in response for support)
63: 
64: == RESPONSE FORMAT ==
65: 
66: All responses wrapped:
67: {
68:   "success": true|false,
69:   "data": <payload>|null,
70:   "error": null|{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} },
71:   "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" }
72: }
73: 
74: == WEBHOOKS (v2.2 feature) ==
75: 
76: POST /webhooks - create webhook
77: body: { url: string, events: ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"], secret: string (optional, for HMAC signing) }
78: 
79: GET /webhooks - list webhooks
80: DELETE /webhooks/{id} - remove webhook
81: 
82: Webhook payload:
83: {
84:   "event": "event.type",
85:   "timestamp": "ISO8601",
86:   "data": { <event specific> }
87: }
88: 
89: If secret provided, we send X-Webhook-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 of body
90: 
91: == RATE LIMITS ==
92: 
93: Free tier: 100 requests/minute, 10000/day
94: Pro tier: 1000 requests/minute, unlimited daily
95: Enterprise: custom
96: 
97: Headers returned:
98: X-RateLimit-Limit: <max>
99: X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining>
100: X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix timestamp>
101: 
102: == SDK notes ==
103: 
104: Python SDK wraps all this, handles auth refresh automatically
105: JS SDK in beta - dont document yet
106: Java SDK abandoned - dont mention
107: 
108: == CHANGELOG snippets ==
109: 
110: v2.2.0 (2024-12-15)
111: - Added webhooks
112: - Fixed: sync jobs sometimes stuck in "running"
113: - Improved: bulk insert now 3x faster
114: 
115: v2.1.0 (2024-11-01)
116: - BREAKING: Switched to JWT auth (API keys deprecated, removed in v3)
117: - Added incremental sync mode
118: - Fixed: rate limit headers missing on 429 responses
119: 
120: v2.0.0 (2024-09-15)
121: - Complete rewrite
122: - New endpoint structure
123: - Added job queue for async operations
124: 
125: == MISC ==
126: 
127: Base URL: https://api.datasync.io/v2
128: Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2 (resets daily, fake data ok)
129: 
130: Content-Type must be application/json for all POST/PUT/PATCH
131: 
132: CORS enabled for *.datasync.io domains, customers can request whitelist
133: 
134: OpenAPI spec is auto-generated but has bugs - dont use directly, needs manual cleanup

(End of file - total 134 lines)
</content>", "type": "text"}]

1: # Release Notes Template
2: 
3: > Based off https://palantir.quip.com/pzRwAVr1bpzf
4: 
5: Pro-tip: look through the github diff between the previous release to see what's changed. The commit titles should give an outline of what's happened.
6: 
7: ### Upgrade Steps
8: 
9: - List out, as concretely as possible, any steps users have to take when they upgrade beyond just dumping the dependency.
10: - Write pseudocode that highlights what code should change and how.
11: - Call out if users are recommended to upgrade because of known problems with older releases.
12: - Preferably, there's nothing here.
13: 
14: ### Breaking Changes
15: 
16: - A complete list of breaking changes (preferably there are none, unless this is a major version).
17: 
18: ### New Features
19: 
20: - Describe the new feature and when/why to use it. Add some pictures! Call out any caveats/warnings? Is it a beta feature?
21: 
22: ### Bug Fixes
23: 
24: - Call out any existing feature/functionality that now works as intended or expected.
25: 
26: ### Improvements
27: 
28: - Improvements/enhancements to a workflow, performance, logging, error messaging, or user experience
29: 
30: ### Other Changes
31: 
32: - Other miscellaneous changes that don't fit into any of the above categories. Try to leave this empty - ideally, all changes fit into the categories above

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Normalize a delimited data file (CSV/TSV) whose cells may contain
3: inner-delimited multi-value fields, and report the counts needed to
4: reconcile a deliverable against its source.
5: 
6: Usage:
7:   python3 scripts/normalize_delimited.py <file.csv> [--delimiter ,] [--inner ;]
8:       [--fields col1,col2] [--out out.json] [--markdown] [--max-col-width 40]
9: 
10: Behavior:
11:   * Parses with the csv module (quoted fields handled correctly).
12:   * If --inner is given, every cell (or only --fields columns) that contains
13:     the inner delimiter is split into a list; a cell without it stays as-is.
14:   * Prints: row count, column list, per-column non-empty counts, per-column
15:     count of cells containing the inner delimiter, and duplicate-key check on
16:     the first column if --key is given.
17:   * With --out, writes a JSON array of row objects (inner-split values as lists).
18:   * With --markdown, prints a markdown table of the normalized rows.
19: 
20: Exit code 0 on success; row/cell counts are printed on stdout for reuse.
21: """
22: 
23: import argparse
24: import csv
25: import json
26: import sys
27: 
28: 
29: def main():
30:     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Normalize delimited data with inner multi-value cells.")
31:     ap.add_argument("path", nargs="?", default="-", help="input file, '-' for stdin")
32:     ap.add_argument("--delimiter", default=",", help="field delimiter (default ',')")
33:     ap.add_argument("--inner", default=None, help="inner delimiter for multi-value cells, e.g. ';'")
34:     ap.add_argument("--fields", default=None, help="comma-separated column names to inner-split (default: any)")
35:     ap.add_argument("--key", default=None, help="column to check for duplicate values")
36:     ap.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="write normalized rows as JSON to this path")
37:     ap.add_argument("--markdown", action="store_true", help="also print a markdown table")
38:     ap.add_argument("--max-col-width", type=int, default=40, help="markdown cell truncation width")
39:     args = ap.parse_args()
40: 
41:     handle = sys.stdin if args.path == "-" else open(args.path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig")
42:     try:
43:         reader = csv.DictReader(handle, delimiter=args.delimiter)
44:         rows = [dict(r) for r in reader]
45:         columns = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
46:     finally:
47:         if handle is not sys.stdin:
48:             handle.close()
49: 
50:     if not rows:
51:         print("ROW_COUNT 0")
52:         print("WARNING: no data rows parsed - check the delimiter")
53:         return 1
54: 
55:     split_fields = set(args.fields.split(",")) if args.fields else None
56:     inner_counts = {c: 0 for c in columns}
57:     normalized = []
58:     for row in rows:
59:         out = {}
60:         for col in columns:
61:             val = (row.get(col) or "").strip()
62:             if args.inner and val and args.inner in val and (split_fields is None or col in split_fields):
63:                 inner_counts[col] += 1
64:                 out[col] = [part.strip() for part in val.split(args.inner) if part.strip() != ""]
65:             else:
66:                 out[col] = val
67:         normalized.append(out)
68: 
69:     print("ROW_COUNT", len(normalized))
70:     print("COLUMNS", "|".join(columns))
71:     for col in columns:
72:         nonempty = sum(1 for r in normalized if r[col])
73:         print("FILLED\t%s\t%d/%d" % (col, nonempty, len(normalized)))
74:     if args.inner:
75:         for col, n in inner_counts.items():
76:             if n:
77:                 print("INNER_SPLIT\t%s\t%d" % (col, n))
78:     if args.key:
79:         if args.key not in columns:
80:             print("WARNING: key column %r not found" % args.key)
81:         else:
82:             seen, dupes = set(), []
83:             for r in normalized:
84:                 k = r[args.key]
85:                 ident = tuple(k) if isinstance(k, list) else (k,)
86:                 if ident in seen:
87:                     dupes.append(str(ident))
88:                 seen.add(ident)
89:             print("DUPLICATE_KEYS", len(dupes), "; ".join(dupes[:5]))
90: 
91:     if args.out:
92:         with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
93:             json.dump(normalized, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
94:         print("WROTE_JSON", args.out)
95: 
96:     if args.markdown:
97:         def cell(v):
98:             text = "; ".join(v) if isinstance(v, list) else str(v)
99:             text = text.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ")
100:             if len(text) > args.max_col_width:
101:                 text = text[: args.max_col_width - 1] + "\u2026"
102:             return text
103: 
104:         print("| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |")
105:         print("|" + "|".join(["---"] * len(columns)) + "|")
106:         for r in normalized:
107:             print("| " + " | ".join(cell(r[c]) for c in columns) + " |")
108:     return 0
109: 
110: 
111: if __name__ == "__main__":
112:     sys.exit(main())

Call the API with the access token\ncurl -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...\" \\\n     https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets\n```\n\n### 3.6 Before/after: token lifecycle handling\n\nLong-running processes must refresh proactively or recover from expiry. 60:   # refresh 60s before expiry\n            self._login_or_refresh()\n        return self.access\n\n    def _login_or_refresh(self):\n        if self.refresh_tok:\n            r = requests.post(f\"{BASE}/auth/refresh\",\n                              json={\"refresh_token\": self.refresh_tok})\n        else:\n            r = requests.post(f\"{BASE}/auth/login\",\n                              json={\"email\": self.email, \"password\": self.password})\n        r.raise_for_status()\n        d = r.json()[\"data\"]\n        self.access, self.refresh_tok = d[\"access_token\"], d[\"refresh_token\"]\n        self.expires_at = time.time() + 55 * 60  # access tokens last ~1 hour\n\nAUTH = Auth(\"you@example.com\", \"...\")\n\ndef call(method, path, **kw):\n    headers = kw.pop(\"headers\", {})\n    headers[\"Authorization\"] = f\"Bearer {AUTH.token()}\"\n    r = requests.request(method, f\"{BASE}{path}\", headers=headers, **kw)\n    if r.status_code == 401:                 # token expired mid-flight: refresh once, retry\n        AUTH._login_or_refresh()\n        headers[\"Authorization\"] = f\"Bearer {AUTH.token()}\"\n        r = requests.request(method, f\"{BASE}{path}\", headers=headers, **kw)\n    return r\n```\n\nHandle these refresh-path responses explicitly:\n\n| Response from `POST /auth/refresh` | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| `200` | New tokens issued | Swap tokens in storage |\n| `400` | Refresh token invalid | Re-login with credentials |\n| `401` | Refresh token expired (older than 7 days) | Re-login with credentials |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Incremental sync (added in v2.1 — commonly missed)\n\n`POST /datasets/{id}/sync` existed in v2.0, so many integrators never re-read its docs. What changed in v2.1: the endpoint gained an **`incremental` mode** that transfers only what changed since the last successful sync, instead of re-syncing the entire dataset.\n\n**Key facts:**\n\n- `mode` accepts `full` or `incremental`; **the default is `full`** — you must opt in explicitly on every request.\n- The call is asynchronous: a `202` response means the job was accepted. Exchange credentials once, store both tokens, refresh proactively before the ~1 hour access-token expiry.\n3. For large fleets, use the staged rollout in Section 3.4 — parallel auth support means API-key services keep working while JWT services come online one by one.\n4. Stop creating new API keys today; complete the switchover before v3 removes key support.\n\n**Before/after code:** Section 3.5 and 3.6.\n\n### Scenario 2 — Webhook subscribed to `dataset.deleted` never fires\n\n**Symptom.** A webhook registered for `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `dataset.deleted`, `sync.completed`, and `sync.failed` receives callbacks for everything except deletions. Datasets disappear from the active list, but no deletion event arrives.\n\n**Root cause.** `dataset.deleted` is **not an implemented event**. `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a **soft delete** (archive): the dataset's archived flag is set and a **`dataset.updated`** event is emitted. The callback *is* being sent — just under a different event name.\n\n**Concrete solution.**\n\n1. Remove `dataset.deleted` from your event subscription; it is not a valid event (valid events: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed`).\n2. Subscribe to `dataset.updated` and inspect the dataset's archived flag in the payload to distinguish archival from ordinary updates (Section 5.3).\n3. Remember the asymmetry: datasets archive (soft), individual records delete permanently (hard) — and record deletion emits no dataset-level event.\n\n### Scenario 3 — Rate limited after ~20 bulk inserts despite a 100 req/min plan limit\n\n**Symptom.** On the Free tier, standard `GET` traffic sails along at up to 100 requests/minute, but a bulk insert job starts receiving `429` after roughly 20 requests.\n\n**Root cause.** Rate limits are enforced **per category**, not just per plan. Bulk record inserts belong to the `bulk` category, which on the Free tier allows **20 requests/minute** — independent of the 100 req/min standard budget.\n\n**Concrete solution.**\n\n1. Batch up to 1,000 records per request (Section 6) — fewer, larger requests fit the bulk budget.\n2. Read `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp) from responses and pace the job accordingly; on `429`, wait until `X-RateLimit-Reset` before retrying.\n3. Design scheduled sync jobs around the per-category budgets in `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Compatibility notes and deprecations\n\n| Item | Status | Details |\n|---|---|---|\n| API key authentication | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Still functional during the transition window; removal planned for v3. Migrate to JWT. |\n| `GET /me/api-keys` | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Legacy key listing. Do not build new integrations on it. |\n| `POST /me/api-keys` | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Legacy key creation. Do not create new keys. |\n| Response envelope | Unchanged | `{ success, data, error, meta }` since v2.0 |\n| Error semantics | Unchanged | `400` validation (with field-level `errors` array), `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `422`, `429`, `500` |\n| v2.0 data endpoints | Unchanged | All 16 operations added in v2.0 behave the same in v2.2 |\n\nNew since v2.0: 4 auth/account operations (v2.1) and 4 webhook operations (v2.2) — 24 operations in total across the API.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Quick reference: v2.0 → v2.2 cheat sheet\n\n| v2.0 pattern | v2.2 replacement |\n|---|---|\n| API key in every request header | `POST /auth/login` → `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`, refresh before ~1 h expiry |\n| Full sync on every run | `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` with `\"mode\": \"incremental\"` |\n| Polling `GET /jobs/{job_id}` in a loop | Subscribe to `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhooks (poll as fallback) |\n| Polling datasets for changes | Subscribe to `dataset.created` / `dataset.updated` |\n| Expecting a `dataset.deleted` event | Handle `dataset.updated` + archived flag (soft delete) |\n| One request per record insert | Batch arrays up to 1,000 records per `POST /datasets/{id}/records` |\n| Ignoring `429` (retry immediately) | Back off using `X-RateLimit-Reset`; respect per-category budgets |\n"}", "type": "tool_call"}]

Formatting follows the Swagger-inspired Markdown style (collapsible endpoint sections, parameter tables, response tables, cURL examples).\n\n**Base URL:** `https://api.datasync.io/v2`\n**Sandbox:** `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2` (resets daily)\n\n---\n\n## Conventions\n\n### Authentication\n\nAll endpoints require authentication unless marked *public*. Send a JWT access token in the `Authorization` header:\n\n```\nAuthorization: Bearer \n```\n\nObtain tokens via `POST /auth/login`; refresh via `POST /auth/refresh`. Access tokens live ~1 hour, refresh tokens 7 days. Legacy API key authentication is **deprecated** (removal planned for v3) — see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`.\n\n### Request format\n\n`Content-Type: application/json` is required for all `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` requests.\n\n### Response envelope\n\nEvery response is wrapped in a standard envelope:\n\n```json\n{\n \"success\": true,\n \"data\": {},\n \"error\": null,\n \"meta\": { \"request_id\": \"uuid\", \"timestamp\": \"ISO8601\" }\n}\n```\n\nOn failure, `success` is `false`, `data` is `null`, and `error` is an object: `{ \"code\": \"ERR_CODE\", \"message\": \"Human readable\", \"details\": {} }`. Validation failures (`400`) include a field-level `errors` array. Server errors (`500`) include a `request_id` in `meta` — include it when contacting support.\n\n### Error codes\n\n| HTTP code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `400` | Bad request — validation failed; body contains field-specific messages |\n| `401` | Not authenticated |\n| `403` | Forbidden — authenticated but not authorized |\n| `404` | Not found |\n| `409` | Conflict (e.g., duplicate dataset name) |\n| `422` | Unprocessable entity — business rule violation |\n| `429` | Rate limited |\n| `500` | Server error |\n\n### Rate limits\n\nRequests are counted in three categories: **standard**, **bulk**, and **sync**. Every response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp) headers; on `429`, wait until the reset time before retrying. See `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md` for the full per-tier matrix.\n\n### Pagination\n\nList endpoints accept `page` (default `1`) and `limit` (default `20`, maximum `100`).\n\n---\n\n## Endpoint inventory\n\n| # | Method | Endpoint | Rate category | Added | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `POST` | `/auth/login` | standard | v2.1.0 | active (public) |\n| 2 | `POST` | `/auth/refresh` | standard | v2.1.0 | active (public) |\n| 3 | `POST` | `/auth/logout` | standard | v2.1.0 | active |\n| 4 | `GET` | `/datasets` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 5 | `POST` | `/datasets` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 6 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 7 | `PUT` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 8 | `DELETE` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active (soft delete) |\n| 9 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}/records` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 10 | `POST` | `/datasets/{id}/records` | **bulk** | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 11 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 12 | `PATCH` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 13 | `DELETE` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active (hard delete) |\n| 14 | `POST` | `/datasets/{id}/sync` | **sync** | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 15 | `GET` | `/jobs/{job_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 16 | `GET` | `/webhooks` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 17 | `POST` | `/webhooks` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 18 | `GET` | `/webhooks/{id}` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 19 | `DELETE` | `/webhooks/{id}` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 20 | `GET` | `/me` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 21 | `PATCH` | `/me` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 22 | `GET` | `/me/api-keys` | standard | v2.0.0 | **DEPRECATED (v2.1)** |\n| 23 | `POST` | `/me/api-keys` | standard | v2.0.0 | **DEPRECATED (v2.1)** |\n| 24 | `GET` | `/me/usage` | standard | v2.1.0 | active |\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Authentication\n\n#### Authenticate and obtain tokens\n\n
\n POST /auth/login (authenticate user and get tokens — public)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------|\n> | `email` | required | string | Account email |\n> | `password` | required | string | Account password |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|--------------------------------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Tokens returned (`access_token`, `refresh_token`) |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid credentials |\n> | `429` | `application/json` | Too many attempts — back off and retry later |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -d '{\"email\":\"you@example.com\",\"password\":\"secret\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/login\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Refresh an access token\n\n
\n POST /auth/refresh (exchange a refresh token for new tokens — public)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|------------------------|\n> | `refresh_token` | required | string | Current refresh token |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|-----------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | New tokens issued |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid token |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Expired token — log in again |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -d '{\"refresh_token\":\"d9f0c1...\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/refresh\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Invalidate tokens\n\n
\n POST /auth/logout (invalidate tokens — requires auth)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|\n> | `refresh_token` | optional | string | Specific token to invalidate; if omitted, **all** tokens for the user are invalidated |\n\n*(Request body — JSON, optional)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"refresh_token\":\"d9f0c1...\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/logout\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Datasets\n\n#### List datasets\n\n
\n GET /datasets (list all datasets for the authenticated user)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------|\n> | `page` | optional | int | Page number (default `1`) |\n> | `limit` | optional | int | Items per page (default `20`, max `100`) |\n> | `status` | optional | string | Filter: `active` \\| `archived` \\| `all` (default `all`) |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|---------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset list |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> \"https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets?page=1&limit=20&status=active\"\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Create a dataset\n\n
\n POST /datasets (create a new dataset)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------|\n> | `name` | required | string | Dataset name — must be 3–100 characters and unique |\n> | `description` | optional | string | Human-readable description |\n> | `tags` | optional | array | List of tags |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `409` | `application/json` | Duplicate name |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"name\":\"Quarterly metrics\",\"description\":\"Q4 data\",\"tags\":[\"finance\"]}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Get a dataset\n\n
\n GET /datasets/{id} (get a single dataset by ID)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID |\n\nReturns `404` if the dataset does not exist or is not owned by the authenticated user.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|-------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Update a dataset\n\n
\n PUT /datasets/{id} (update a dataset)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `name` | optional | string | New name (3–100 chars, unique) |\n> | `description` | optional | string | New description |\n> | `tags` | optional | array | New tag list |\n\n*(Request body — JSON; same fields as create, all optional)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X PUT -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"description\":\"Updated description\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Archive (soft-delete) a dataset\n\n
\n DELETE /datasets/{id} (archive a dataset — soft delete)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------|-----------|-----------|----------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID |\n\n> **This is a soft delete.** The dataset's archived flag is set; it is not permanently removed and remains retrievable via `GET /datasets?status=archived`. Archiving emits a **`dataset.updated`** webhook event — there is no `dataset.deleted` event.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X DELETE -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### List records in a dataset\n\n
\n GET /datasets/{id}/records (list records in a dataset)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `page` | optional | int | Page number (default `1`) |\n> | `limit` | optional | int | Items per page (default `20`, max `100`) |\n> | `sort` | optional | string | Field name to sort by |\n> | `order` | optional | string | `asc` (default) \\| `desc` |\n> | `filter` | optional | string | JSON-encoded filter query |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|----------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Record list |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> \"https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records?page=1&limit=20&sort=created_at&order=desc&filter=%7B%22status%22%3A%22active%22%7D\"\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Add records to a dataset (bulk-capable)\n\n
\n POST /datasets/{id}/records (add records — single object or array, max 1,000 per request)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-----------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `records` | required | array | Records to add; a single record object is also accepted. **Max 1,000 records per request.** |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n> **Rate limit category: `bulk`.** This endpoint is counted against the bulk rate limit category, which is separate from (and lower than) the standard budget — e.g., 20 requests/minute on the Free tier. Batch records up to the 1,000-per-request maximum.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|----------------------|\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"records\":[{\"field1\":\"a\"},{\"field1\":\"b\"}]}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Get a single record\n\n
\n GET /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (get a single record)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID |\n> | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Record |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Update a single record\n\n
\n PATCH /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (partial update of a single record)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID (path) |\n> | *field:value pairs* | required | object | Partial record object — only the fields to change |\n\n*(Request body — JSON; partial update only)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X PATCH -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"status\":\"reviewed\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Delete a single record\n\n
\n DELETE /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (delete a single record — hard delete)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID |\n> | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID |\n\n> Unlike dataset deletion (archive/soft delete), **record deletion is a hard delete** and cannot be undone.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X DELETE -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Trigger a sync\n\n
\n POST /datasets/{id}/sync (trigger an async sync job with an external source)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `source_id` | required | string | External source identifier |\n> | `mode` | optional | string | `full` (default) \\| `incremental` — incremental transfers only changes since the last successful sync |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n> The call is asynchronous: a `202` response means the job was accepted; track it via `GET /jobs/{job_id}` or the `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhook events.\n>\n> **Rate limit category: `sync`.** Sync requests are counted in their own category, separate from the standard budget.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|--------------------|\n> | `202` | `application/json` | Job started (returns job identifier) |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid source |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"source_id\":\"src_123\",\"mode\":\"incremental\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/sync\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Jobs\n\n#### Check async job status\n\n
\n GET /jobs/{job_id} (check the status of an async job, e.g. a sync)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|-------------|\n> | `job_id` | required | string | Job identifier returned by the operation that started it |\n\n##### Response payload\n\n`data` contains: `status` (`pending` | `running` | `completed` | `failed`), `progress` (0–100), `error` (string or `null`).\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Job status |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Job not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/jobs/job_789\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Webhooks\n\nWebhook subscriptions push notifications to your HTTPS endpoint when events occur. Supported events:\n\n| Event | Fired when |\n|---|---|\n| `dataset.created` | A dataset is created |\n| `dataset.updated` | A dataset is updated **or archived** (soft delete) |\n| `sync.completed` | A sync job completes successfully |\n| `sync.failed` | A sync job fails |\n\n> **There is no `dataset.deleted` event.** `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a soft delete (archive) that emits `dataset.updated`.\n\nPayload shape for every delivery:\n\n```json\n{\n \"event\": \"dataset.updated\",\n \"timestamp\": \"ISO8601\",\n \"data\": { \"...\" : \"event-specific fields\" }\n}\n```\n\n#### List webhooks\n\n
\n GET /webhooks (list configured webhooks)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> None\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|--------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook list |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Create a webhook\n\n

Before you start: collect diagnostics\n\nEvery API response includes a `meta` object:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": false,\n  \"data\": null,\n  \"error\": { \"code\": \"ERR_CODE\", \"message\": \"Human readable\", \"details\": {} },\n  \"meta\": { \"request_id\": \"b2c1...\", \"timestamp\": \"2024-12-15T10:00:00Z\" }\n}\n```\n\n- Always capture **`meta.request_id`** — support uses it to locate the exact request in server logs.\n- `400` validation failures include an `errors` array with field-specific messages — read it before guessing.\n- `500` responses are logged server-side; retry with backoff and provide the `request_id` if the problem persists.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Authentication error diagnostics\n\n### 1.1 `401 Unauthorized` — decision tree\n\nWork down the list in order:\n\n1. **Is the `Authorization` header present and well-formed?**\n   Correct format: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.\n   - Missing header → `401`.\n   - Wrong scheme (e.g., sending the token without the `Bearer` prefix, or a legacy API key credential in a bearer-style header) → `401`. This is the single most common cause of 401s reported after upgrading from v2.0.\n2. **Has the access token expired?** Access tokens live **~1 hour**. If your process caches a token across long runs, refresh it (`POST /auth/refresh`) proactively — don't wait for the 401.\n3. **Was the token invalidated?** `POST /auth/logout` invalidates tokens — and if called **without** a `refresh_token` in the body, it invalidates **all** tokens for the user. If another team member or job ran a full logout, every outstanding token stops working. Re-login.\n4. **Is the refresh token the problem?** Distinguish the two refresh failures:\n   - `400` from `POST /auth/refresh` → the refresh token is **invalid** — re-login with credentials.\n   - `401` from `POST /auth/refresh` → the refresh token has **expired** (they last **7 days**) — re-login with credentials.\n5. **Still authenticating with a legacy API key?** Keys remain functional during the deprecation window (removal planned for v3), but they are deprecated. If a request with a key returns 401, verify the key is still listed via `GET /me/api-keys` and that your client is sending the credential exactly as configured in your v2.0 integration. Plan the JWT migration regardless — see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`.\n\n### 1.2 `401` vs `403` — which one means what\n\n| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| `401` | Not authenticated — the server cannot verify who you are | Fix the token (sections 1.1) |\n| `403` | Forbidden — authenticated, but not authorized for this resource | Use credentials/resource your user actually owns |\n\n**Known behavior:** in some cases an authorization failure (valid token, insufficient permissions) is reported as `401` instead of `403`. Back off and retry later; do not loop login attempts in a retry storm. Batch services behind a shared token service so 40+ processes are not each performing logins.\n\n### 1.4 Auth error quick reference\n\n| Where | Response | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Any endpoint | `401` | Not authenticated / token expired / token invalidated | Check header, refresh or re-login |\n| Any endpoint | `403` | Authenticated but not authorized | Check resource ownership/permissions |\n| `POST /auth/login` | `400` | Invalid credentials | Check email/password |\n| `POST /auth/login` | `429` | Too many attempts | Back off; centralize token acquisition |\n| `POST /auth/refresh` | `400` | Invalid refresh token | Re-login |\n| `POST /auth/refresh` | `401` | Refresh token expired (7 days) | Re-login |\n\n---\n\n## 2. Rate limiting\n\n### 2.1 Categories — the part most integrations miss\n\nRate limits are enforced **per category**, not only per plan. Every endpoint belongs to exactly one category:\n\n| Category | Endpoints counted | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `standard` | All endpoints **except** the two below (22 of 24 operations) | The default budget |\n| `bulk` | `POST /datasets/{id}/records` only | Separate budget, **lower** than standard |\n| `sync` | `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` only | Separate budget, independent of standard |\n\nSo on the Free tier, 60 standard `GET` requests plus 25 bulk inserts in the same minute does **not** fit: the 60 are fine, the 25 bulk requests exceed the 20/min bulk budget and the 21st onward get `429` — even though you are far under 100 req/min overall.\n\n### 2.2 Limits by tier\n\n| Tier | Standard | Bulk | Sync | Daily cap |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Free | 100 req/min | **20 req/min** | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | 10,000 req/day |\n| Pro | 1,000 req/min | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | None |\n| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom |\n\nThe authoritative limit for your plan and category is always exposed in the `X-RateLimit-Limit` response header — read it once from a live call rather than hardcoding assumptions.\n\n### 2.3 Rate limit response headers\n\nEvery response (success or `429`) carries:\n\n| Header | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Maximum requests per window for that category |\n| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests remaining in the current window |\n| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp when the window resets |\n\n> Headers on `429` responses have been reliable since v2.1 (a v2.0 defect omitted them). Webhook issues\n\n### 3.1 Not receiving callbacks — checklist\n\n1. **List your actual subscriptions** with `GET /webhooks` and compare the `events` array to what you expect.\n2. **Are you subscribed to an event that doesn't exist?** The valid events are exactly: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed`. Common migration pitfalls (v2.0 → v2.2)\n\nCompiled from recurring support patterns. Each row states the mistake, the observable symptom, and the correct behavior.\n\n| # | Pitfall | Symptom | Correct behavior |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Assuming old auth still works unchanged | `401` after upgrade | JWT is the standard since v2.1; API keys are deprecated but still work during the window — verify header format first (`MIGRATION_GUIDE` §3) |\n| 2 | Caching access tokens beyond their ~1 h lifetime | Sudden `401`s after an hour of operation | Refresh proactively or retry once on 401 after refreshing |\n| 3 | Subscribing to `dataset.deleted` | No callbacks when datasets are archived | Event doesn't exist; `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a soft delete that emits `dataset.updated` |\n| 4 | Treating dataset deletion as permanent | Dataset \"gone\" but still in storage | Soft delete sets the archived flag; retrieve with `GET /datasets?status=archived`. Record deletion (`.../records/{record_id}`) **is** a hard delete |\n| 5 | Hammering bulk inserts | `429` after ~20 requests on Free tier | Bulk is its own rate category (20 req/min on Free); batch up to 1,000 records per request |\n| 6 | Assuming one global rate limit | Unexpected `429` while \"well under the limit\" | Limits are per category: standard / bulk / sync |\n| 7 | Requesting `limit` > 100 on list endpoints | Truncated results or validation error | `limit` defaults to 20, **max 100**; page through with `page` |\n| 8 | Invalid dataset names | `400` on create | Name must be 3–100 characters |\n| 9 | Duplicate dataset names | `409` on create | Names must be unique — catch 409 and reuse/update the existing dataset |\n| 10 | Missing `Content-Type: application/json` | `400` on POST/PUT/PATCH | The header is required for all body-sending requests |\n| 11 | Sending `filter` as an unencoded object | Filter ignored or `400` | The `filter` parameter is **JSON-encoded** (URL-encode it in query strings) |\n| 12 | Assuming `sort` descends by default | \"Wrong\" ordering | `order` defaults to `asc` — set `order=desc` explicitly |\n| 13 | Running syncs in `full` mode out of habit | Slow, heavy sync jobs | `mode` defaults to `full`; pass `incremental` for recurring syncs (v2.1 feature) |\n| 14 | Treating the `202` from `/sync` as completion | Missing data; no job tracking | `202` = job accepted. Track via `GET /jobs/{job_id}` or `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhooks |\n| 15 | Missing rate limit headers on 429s (v2.0 behavior) | Retry logic without backoff timing | Fixed in v2.1 — headers are present on all responses, including `429` |\n| 16 | Ignoring `422` | Confusing business-rule failures with validation bugs | `400` = field validation (see `errors` array); `422` = business rule violation |\n| 17 | Retrying `500` immediately and repeatedly | Extended disruption | Back off; include `meta.request_id` in the support ticket |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Escalated scenario walkthroughs\n\nThe three Customer Success escalations that triggered this documentation, anonymized, with the resolution paths.\n\n### Scenario A — \"JWT migration breaking our integration\" (Enterprise, dozens of microservices)\n\n- **Symptom:** `401` errors after upgrading; API keys still visible in the dashboard; legacy key endpoints still return 200; no published transition guidance.\n- **Diagnosis:** v2.1 switched to JWT and deprecated API keys. 1: # DataSync API — Migration Guide: v2.0 → v2.2
2: 
3: This guide is for teams whose integrations were built against **DataSync API v2.0** and are moving to **v2.2**. The path crosses two releases — v2.1.0 (2024-11-01) and v2.2.0 (2024-12-15) — and the most impactful change on that path is the switch from API key authentication to JWT.
4: 
5: **Companion documents:**
6: 
7: - `API_REFERENCE.md` — full endpoint documentation for v2.2
8: - `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md` — diagnostics for auth, rate limit, and webhook issues
9: - `RELEASE_NOTES_v2.2.md` — what shipped in v2.2.0
10: 
11: **Environments**
12: 
13: | Environment | Base URL | Notes |
14: |---|---|---|
15: | Production | `https://api.datasync.io/v2` | |
16: | Sandbox | `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2` | Resets daily; safe for migration testing |
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. What changed between v2.0 and v2.2
21: 
22: | Release | Date | Change | Impact on v2.0 integrations |
23: |---|---|---|---|
24: | v2.1.0 | 2024-11-01 | **JWT authentication** replaces API keys (keys deprecated; removal planned for v3) | **Action required** — plan and execute an auth migration |
25: | v2.1.0 | 2024-11-01 | **Incremental sync mode** added to `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` | Optional — significant efficiency gain, easy to miss |
26: | v2.1.0 | 2024-11-01 | Rate limit headers are now returned on `429` responses | Enables proper backoff handling |
27: | v2.2.0 | 2024-12-15 | **Webhooks** (event subscriptions with optional HMAC signatures) | Optional — replaces polling patterns |
28: | v2.2.0 | 2024-12-15 | Fixed: sync jobs occasionally stuck in `running` status | Reliability improvement |
29: | v2.2.0 | 2024-12-15 | Bulk record inserts are ~3x faster | Performance improvement |
30: 
31: **No new breaking changes were introduced in v2.2.0 itself.** The one breaking change on the v2.0 → v2.2 path is the authentication switch in v2.1. The response envelope, error codes, and all v2.0 data endpoints behave the same in v2.2.
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## 2. Upgrade path overview
36: 
37: Work through these steps in order. Each maps to a section below.
38: 
39: 1. **Test in the sandbox first.** The sandbox resets daily, so you can iterate freely against fake data.
40: 2. **Plan the authentication migration** (Section 3). This is the only mandatory work: legacy API keys are deprecated and will be removed in v3. Both auth methods work side by side during the deprecation window, so you can migrate in phases.
41: 3. **Adopt incremental sync** where you trigger syncs (Section 4). This capability shipped in v2.1 and is opt-in per request — many v2.0 integrators never noticed it.
42: 4. **Evaluate webhooks** for event-driven patterns (Section 5) — new in v2.2.
43: 5. **Revisit bulk insert batching** (Section 6) — inserts are faster in v2.2, and bulk requests draw from their own rate limit category.
44: 6. **Verify rate limit handling** — make sure your client reads `X-RateLimit-*` headers and backs off correctly on `429` (see `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md`).
45: 
46: ### Pre-migration checklist
47: 
48: - [ ] Integration tested against `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2`
49: - [ ] Inventory of every service/cron job/script that calls the API with a legacy API key
50: - [ ] JWT login + refresh flow implemented and tested (Section 3.5–3.6)
51: - [ ] Decision recorded for each service: migrate now or during the deprecation window (Section 3.4)
52: - [ ] Sync calls reviewed for `mode` usage (Section 4)
53: - [ ] Bulk insert chunking reviewed against the 1,000-record-per-request limit (Section 6)
54: - [ ] `429` handler uses `X-RateLimit-Reset` for backoff
55: - [ ] Webhook signature verification implemented if you subscribe to events (Section 5)
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 3. Authentication transition: API keys → JWT
60: 
61: ### 3.1 What changed
62: 
63: - **v2.0** authenticated requests with a long-lived API key sent with every request.
64: - **v2.1** switched to **JWT bearer tokens** obtained from `POST /auth/login`. API keys were deprecated at the same time.
65: - **Deprecation window:** both methods are accepted during the transition period. API keys will be **removed in v3**.
66: - The legacy key management endpoints — `GET /me/api-keys` and `POST /me/api-keys` — still operate, but they are **deprecated** and exist only to support the transition.
67: 
68: ### 3.2 What still works during the deprecation period
69: 
70: A frequent source of confusion: *"the key endpoints still return 200 — are my keys still valid?"*
71: 
72: **Yes.** During the deprecation window:
73: 
74: - Existing API keys continue to authenticate requests.
75: - `GET /me/api-keys` still lists your keys, and `POST /me/api-keys` still creates new ones (both marked deprecated in the API reference).
76: - Do **not** create new API keys for new services or new deployments. New development should use JWT exclusively.
77: 
78: The continued operation of these endpoints is deliberate: it is what makes a phased migration possible. It is **not** a signal that API keys are a supported long-term option.
79: 
80: ### 3.3 JWT quick start
81: 
82: ```
83: POST /auth/login
84: { "email": "you@example.com", "password": "..." }
85: ```
86: 
87: Response:
88: 
89: ```json
90: {
91:   "success": true,
92:   "data": {
93:     "access_token": "eyJhbGciOi...",
94:     "refresh_token": "d9f0c1..."
95:   },
96:   "meta": { "request_id": "b2c1...", "timestamp": "2024-12-15T10:00:00Z" }
97: }
98: ```
99: 
100: Token facts you must design around:
101: 
102: | Token | Lifetime | Used for |
103: |---|---|---|
104: | `access_token` | ~1 hour | `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` header on every API call |
105: | `refresh_token` | 7 days | `POST /auth/refresh` to obtain a new access token (and new tokens) |
106: 
107: Notes:
108: 
109: - `POST /auth/refresh` takes the `refresh_token` in the request body — no credentials required.
110: - `POST /auth/logout` invalidates tokens. If you omit the `refresh_token` in the body, **all** tokens for the user are invalidated.
111: - `429` can be returned by `POST /auth/login` after too many attempts — back off and retry later.
112: 
113: ### 3.4 Decision criteria for the deprecation period
114: 
115: Because both methods work during the window, the right question is not *“can we defer?”* but *“which services should move first?”* Use these criteria:
116: 
117: | Factor | Migrate now | Defer (staged) |
118: |---|---|---|
119: | Number of services using the key | A handful | Dozens of microservices — migrate in phases |
120: | Refresh handling in your stack | Token storage/refresh already implemented | Needs infra work — start now, finish before v3 |
121: | Security posture requirements | High — short-lived JWTs reduce the blast radius of leaked credentials | Low-sensitivity internal tooling can move last |
122: | New services or rewrite in progress | Always JWT — never build on keys | — |
123: | Creating new API keys | Stop immediately (`POST /me/api-keys` is deprecated) | — |
124: | Deadline | — | **All services must be off API keys before v3**, when key support is removed |
125: 
126: **Recommended staged approach for large fleets** (for example, an enterprise with dozens of microservices sharing one key):
127: 
128: 1. Keep the existing API key running — nothing breaks during the window.
129: 2. Implement a shared token service (or use your platform's secret manager) that performs login + refresh once and hands short-lived access tokens to services. This avoids 47 services each implementing refresh logic.
130: 3. Migrate services in waves: start with low-risk read-only consumers, finish with write-heavy services.
131: 4. After each wave, confirm no 401 spikes, then stop using the key in that wave's services.
132: 5. When the last wave is done, remove the key from all configuration — do not wait for the v3 removal date.
133: 
134: ### 3.5 Before/after: authenticating a request
135: 
136: **Before — v2.0 pattern (API key sent with every request; header name as configured in your v2.0 integration):**
137: 
138: ```bash
139: curl -H "X-API-Key: ak_live_xxxx" \
140:      https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets
141: ```
142: 
143: **After — v2.2 pattern (JWT bearer token):**
144: 
145: ```bash
146: # 1. Exchange credentials for tokens (once per hour)
147: curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
148:      -d '{"email":"you@example.com","password":"..."}' \
149:      https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/login
150: 
151: # 2. Call the API with the access token
152: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi..." \
153:      https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets
154: ```
155: 
156: ### 3.6 Before/after: token lifecycle handling
157: 
158: Long-running processes must refresh proactively or recover from expiry. A minimal Python pattern:
159: 
160: **Before (v2.0):** static credential, no lifecycle code.
161: 
162: ```python
163: API_KEY = "ak_live_xxxx"  # set once, never changes
164: 
165: def call(path, **kw):
166:     return requests.get(f"{BASE}/datasets", headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY})
167: ```
168: 
169: **After (v2.2):** login, proactive refresh, and 401 retry.
170: 
171: ```python

176:         self.email, self.password = email, password
177:         self.access = self.refresh_tok = None
178:         self.expires_at = 0
179:

181:         if time.time() > self.expires_at - 60:   # refresh 60s before expiry

183:         return self.access
184: 
185:     def _login_or_refresh(self):
186:         if self.refresh_tok:
187:             r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/auth/refresh",
188:                               json={"refresh_token": self.refresh_tok})
189:         else:
190:             r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/auth/login",
191:                               json={"email": self.email, "password": self.password})
192:         r.raise_for_status()
193:         d = r.json()["data"]
194:         self.access, self.refresh_tok = d["access_token"], d["refresh_token"]
195:         self.expires_at = time.time() + 55 * 60  # access tokens last ~1 hour
196: 
197: AUTH = Auth("you@example.com", "...")
198: 
199: def call(method, path, **kw):
200:     headers = kw.pop("headers", {})
201:     headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {AUTH.token()}"
202:     r = requests.request(method, f"{BASE}{path}", headers=headers, **kw)
203:     if r.status_code == 401:                 # token expired mid-flight: refresh once, retry
204:         AUTH._login_or_refresh()
205:         headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {AUTH.token()}"
206:         r = requests.request(method, f"{BASE}{path}", headers=headers, **kw)
207:     return r
208: ```
209: 
210: Handle these refresh-path responses explicitly:
211: 
212: | Response from `POST /auth/refresh` | Meaning | Action |
213: |---|---|---|
214: | `200` | New tokens issued | Swap tokens in storage |
215: | `400` | Refresh token invalid | Re-login with credentials |
216: | `401` | Refresh token expired (older than 7 days) | Re-login with credentials |
217: 
218: ---
219: 
220: ## 4. Incremental sync (added in v2.1 — commonly missed)
221: 
222: `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` existed in v2.0, so many integrators never re-read its docs. What changed in v2.1: the endpoint gained an **`incremental` mode** that transfers only what changed since the last successful sync, instead of re-syncing the entire dataset.
223: 
224: **Key facts:**
225: 
226: - `mode` accepts `full` or `incremental`; **the default is `full`** — you must opt in explicitly on every request.
227: - The call is asynchronous: a `202` response means the job was accepted. The response body identifies the job; poll `GET /jobs/{job_id}` for `{ "status": "pending" | "running" | "completed" | "failed", "progress": 0-100, "error": string | null }`.
228: - Sync requests draw from the dedicated **sync rate limit category**, separate from standard request limits (see `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md`).
229: - v2.2 also fixed a defect where sync jobs could occasionally remain stuck in `running`.
230: 
231: **Before — v2.0 pattern (full sync every run):**
232: 
233: ```python
234: r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/datasets/{ds_id}/sync",
235:                   headers=auth_headers,
236:                   json={"source_id": "src_123", "mode": "full"})
237: job_id = r.json()["data"]["job_id"]
238: ```
239: 
240: **After — v2.2 pattern (incremental, with job tracking):**
241: 
242: ```python
243: r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/datasets/{ds_id}/sync",
244:                   headers=auth_headers,
245:                   json={"source_id": "src_123", "mode": "incremental"})
246: job_id = r.json()["data"]["job_id"]
247: 
248: # Poll until the job settles
249: while True:
250:     job = requests.get(f"{BASE}/jobs/{job_id}", headers=auth_headers).json()["data"]
251:     if job["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
252:         break
253:     time.sleep(5)
254: ```
255: 
256: With v2.2 you can replace the polling loop entirely by subscribing to the `sync.completed` and `sync.failed` webhook events (Section 5) — poll only as a fallback.
257: 
258: **When to use `incremental`:** any recurring or scheduled sync against a source you already synced before. Use `full` for initial loads, source reconfigurations, or after suspected drift.
259: 
260: ---
261: 
262: ## 5. Webhooks (new in v2.2)
263: 
264: Webhooks let the API notify you when things happen, instead of you polling.
265: 
266: ### 5.1 The event list — and the one event that does *not* exist
267: 
268: | Event | Fired when |
269: |---|---|
270: | `dataset.created` | A dataset is created |
271: | `dataset.updated` | A dataset is updated **or archived** (see below) |
272: | `sync.completed` | A sync job finishes successfully |
273: | `sync.failed` | A sync job fails |
274: 
275: > **Important — there is no `dataset.deleted` event.** `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a **soft delete**: it sets the dataset's archived flag and emits a **`dataset.updated`** event. If your webhook filter includes `dataset.deleted`, it will simply never fire. To detect archival, subscribe to `dataset.updated` and check the dataset's archived/status state in the payload. (Deleting an individual *record* via `DELETE /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` is a hard delete and is not accompanied by a dataset-level event.)
276: 
277: ### 5.2 Getting started
278: 
279: ```
280: POST /webhooks
281: { "url": "https://hooks.example.com/datasync",
282:   "events": ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"],
283:   "secret": "whsec_..." }
284: ```
285: 
286: - `secret` is optional but **strongly recommended**: when set, every delivery includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header containing the HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body, keyed with your secret. Verification steps and reference code are in `API_REFERENCE.md` (Webhooks → Signature verification).
287: - Payload shape for every event:
288: 
289: ```json
290: {
291:   "event": "dataset.updated",
292:   "timestamp": "2024-12-15T10:00:00Z",
293:   "data": { "...": "event-specific fields" }
294: }
295: ```
296: 
297: ### 5.3 Before/after: change detection
298: 
299: **Before (v2.0):** poll the API on a timer to notice changes.
300: 
301: ```python
302: while True:
303:     datasets = requests.get(f"{BASE}/datasets", headers=auth_headers).json()["data"]
304:     diff_against_last_snapshot(datasets)
305:     time.sleep(300)
306: ```
307: 
308: **After (v2.2):** react to events; poll only as a fallback.
309: 
310: ```python
311: @app.post("/datasync")
312: def handle(request):
313:     if not signature_valid(request):          # HMAC-SHA256, see API_REFERENCE.md
314:         return "", 400
315:     body = request.get_json()
316:     if body["event"] == "dataset.updated" and body["data"].get("archived"):
317:         handle_archival(body["data"])          # replaces a "dataset.deleted" handler
318:     elif body["event"] == "sync.completed":
319:         refresh_local_copy(body["data"])
320:     return "", 200
321: ```
322: 
323: ---
324: 
325: ## 6. Bulk record inserts
326: 
327: `POST /datasets/{id}/records` accepts either a single record object or an array of records (**max 1,000 records per request**). In v2.2 bulk inserts are approximately **3x faster**.
328: 
329: One behavior change to be aware of: bulk record inserts draw from a dedicated **bulk rate limit category** with its own — lower — limits, separate from the standard request budget. On the Free tier that is **20 bulk requests per minute**. If your sync jobs post many small batches, they will hit `429` long before the standard limit is reached.
330: 
331: **Before (v2.0):** many small requests.
332: 
333: ```python
334: for record in records:                       # N requests, N chances to be rate limited
335:     requests.post(f"{BASE}/datasets/{ds_id}/records",
336:                   headers=auth_headers, json=record)
337: ```
338: 
339: **After (v2.2):** batch up to 1,000 records per request.
340: 
341: ```python
342: for chunk in chunks(records, 1000):          # ceil(N/1000) requests
343:     requests.post(f"{BASE}/datasets/{ds_id}/records",
344:                   headers=auth_headers, json=chunk)
345: ```
346: 
347: Batching reduces request count (helping you stay inside the bulk rate category) *and* benefits from the v2.2 performance improvement. See `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md` for the full rate limit matrix and retry strategy.
348: 
349: ---
350: 
351: ## 7. Escalated support scenarios, resolved
352: 
353: The three scenarios below came through Customer Success as documentation escalations. They are reproduced here (anonymized) because each one represents a migration pattern other integrators are likely to hit.
354: 
355: ### Scenario 1 — 401 errors after upgrading, with API keys still listed in the dashboard
356: 
357: **Symptom.** After upgrading, requests that worked in v2.0 return `401`. The legacy key management endpoints still respond successfully, which makes it look like nothing changed.
358: 
359: **Root cause.** v2.1 switched the platform to JWT authentication. API keys are deprecated but still accepted during the transition window — so a `401` at this stage almost always means the *request* is malformed for the new auth flow (missing/misnamed header, cached expired credentials), not that the key was revoked.
360: 
361: **Concrete solution.**
362: 
363: 1. Confirm the key still works by listing it via `GET /me/api-keys` (deprecated, but functional).
364: 2. Implement the JWT flow (Section 3.3 / 3.6). Exchange credentials once, store both tokens, refresh proactively before the ~1 hour access-token expiry.
365: 3. For large fleets, use the staged rollout in Section 3.4 — parallel auth support means API-key services keep working while JWT services come online one by one.
366: 4. Stop creating new API keys today; complete the switchover before v3 removes key support.
367: 
368: **Before/after code:** Section 3.5 and 3.6.
369: 
370: ### Scenario 2 — Webhook subscribed to `dataset.deleted` never fires
371: 
372: **Symptom.** A webhook registered for `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `dataset.deleted`, `sync.completed`, and `sync.failed` receives callbacks for everything except deletions. Datasets disappear from the active list, but no deletion event arrives.
373: 
374: **Root cause.** `dataset.deleted` is **not an implemented event**. `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a **soft delete** (archive): the dataset's archived flag is set and a **`dataset.updated`** event is emitted. The callback *is* being sent — just under a different event name.
375: 
376: **Concrete solution.**
377: 
378: 1. Remove `dataset.deleted` from your event subscription; it is not a valid event (valid events: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed`).
379: 2. Subscribe to `dataset.updated` and inspect the dataset's archived flag in the payload to distinguish archival from ordinary updates (Section 5.3).
380: 3. Remember the asymmetry: datasets archive (soft), individual records delete permanently (hard) — and record deletion emits no dataset-level event.
381: 
382: ### Scenario 3 — Rate limited after ~20 bulk inserts despite a 100 req/min plan limit
383: 
384: **Symptom.** On the Free tier, standard `GET` traffic sails along at up to 100 requests/minute, but a bulk insert job starts receiving `429` after roughly 20 requests.
385: 
386: **Root cause.** Rate limits are enforced **per category**, not just per plan. Bulk record inserts belong to the `bulk` category, which on the Free tier allows **20 requests/minute** — independent of the 100 req/min standard budget.
387: 
388: **Concrete solution.**
389: 
390: 1. Batch up to 1,000 records per request (Section 6) — fewer, larger requests fit the bulk budget.
391: 2. Read `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp) from responses and pace the job accordingly; on `429`, wait until `X-RateLimit-Reset` before retrying.
392: 3. Design scheduled sync jobs around the per-category budgets in `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md`.
393: 
394: ---
395: 
396: ## 8. Compatibility notes and deprecations
397: 
398: | Item | Status | Details |
399: |---|---|---|
400: | API key authentication | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Still functional during the transition window; removal planned for v3. Migrate to JWT. |
401: | `GET /me/api-keys` | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Legacy key listing. Do not build new integrations on it. |
402: | `POST /me/api-keys` | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Legacy key creation. Do not create new keys. |
403: | Response envelope | Unchanged | `{ success, data, error, meta }` since v2.0 |
404: | Error semantics | Unchanged | `400` validation (with field-level `errors` array), `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `422`, `429`, `500` |
405: | v2.0 data endpoints | Unchanged | All 16 operations added in v2.0 behave the same in v2.2 |
406: 
407: New since v2.0: 4 auth/account operations (v2.1) and 4 webhook operations (v2.2) — 24 operations in total across the API.
408: 
409: ---
410: 
411: ## 9. Quick reference: v2.0 → v2.2 cheat sheet
412: 
413: | v2.0 pattern | v2.2 replacement |
414: |---|---|
415: | API key in every request header | `POST /auth/login` → `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`, refresh before ~1 h expiry |
416: | Full sync on every run | `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` with `"mode": "incremental"` |
417: | Polling `GET /jobs/{job_id}` in a loop | Subscribe to `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhooks (poll as fallback) |
418: | Polling datasets for changes | Subscribe to `dataset.created` / `dataset.updated` |
419: | Expecting a `dataset.deleted` event | Handle `dataset.updated` + archived flag (soft delete) |
420: | One request per record insert | Batch arrays up to 1,000 records per `POST /datasets/{id}/records` |
421: | Ignoring `429` (retry immediately) | Back off using `X-RateLimit-Reset`; respect per-category budgets |

(End of file - total 421 lines)

1: # Developer Notes - DataSync API
2: # These are internal notes from the dev team - NOT for external publication
3: # Last updated by multiple contributors
4: 
5: == AUTH STUFF ==
6: We use JWT tokens now. Changed from API keys last sprint (v2.1).
7: Token expires in 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
8: Header format: Authorization: Bearer <token>
9: Login endpoint: POST /auth/login - takes email+password, returns tokens
10: Refresh: POST /auth/refresh - takes refresh_token in body
11: 
12: BUG: Sometimes 401 returns instead of 403 when token valid but perms wrong
13: TODO: Fix in next sprint (JIRA-4521)
14: 
15: == DATA ENDPOINTS ==
16: 
17: /datasets - GET list all datasets for user
18: params: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100), status (active|archived|all)
19: returns array of dataset objects
20: 
21: /datasets/{id} - GET single dataset
22: 404 if not found or not owned by user
23: 
24: /datasets - POST create new dataset
25: body: { name: string (required, 3-100 chars), description: string (optional), tags: array }
26: returns created dataset with id
27: 
28: /datasets/{id} - PUT update dataset
29: same body as POST but all fields optional
30: returns updated dataset
31: 
32: /datasets/{id} - DELETE soft delete (sets archived flag)
33: returns 204 no content
34: 
35: /datasets/{id}/records - GET records in dataset
36: pagination same as /datasets list
37: params: sort (field name), order (asc|desc), filter (JSON encoded query)
38: 
39: /datasets/{id}/records - POST add record(s)
40: body can be single object or array for bulk insert
41: max 1000 records per request
42: 
43: /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} - PATCH update single record
44: body: partial record object
45: 
46: /datasets/{id}/sync - POST trigger sync with external source
47: body: { source_id: string, mode: "full"|"incremental" }
48: returns job_id for async tracking
49: 
50: /jobs/{job_id} - GET check job status
51: response: { status: "pending"|"running"|"completed"|"failed", progress: 0-100, error: string|null }
52: 
53: == ERROR CODES ==
54: 
55: 400 - bad request (validation failed) - body has "errors" array with field-specific messages
56: 401 - not authenticated
57: 403 - forbidden (authenticated but not authorized)
58: 404 - not found
59: 409 - conflict (e.g., duplicate name)
60: 422 - unprocessable entity (business rule violation)
61: 429 - rate limited (100 req/min for free tier, 1000 for pro)
62: 500 - server error (we log these, include request_id in response for support)
63: 
64: == RESPONSE FORMAT ==
65: 
66: All responses wrapped:
67: {
68:   "success": true|false,
69:   "data": <payload>|null,
70:   "error": null|{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} },
71:   "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" }
72: }
73: 
74: == WEBHOOKS (v2.2 feature) ==
75: 
76: POST /webhooks - create webhook
77: body: { url: string, events: ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"], secret: string (optional, for HMAC signing) }
78: 
79: GET /webhooks - list webhooks
80: DELETE /webhooks/{id} - remove webhook
81: 
82: Webhook payload:
83: {
84:   "event": "event.type",
85:   "timestamp": "ISO8601",
86:   "data": { <event specific> }
87: }
88: 
89: If secret provided, we send X-Webhook-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 of body
90: 
91: == RATE LIMITS ==
92: 
93: Free tier: 100 requests/minute, 10000/day
94: Pro tier: 1000 requests/minute, unlimited daily
95: Enterprise: custom
96: 
97: Headers returned:
98: X-RateLimit-Limit: <max>
99: X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining>
100: X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix timestamp>
101: 
102: == SDK notes ==
103: 
104: Python SDK wraps all this, handles auth refresh automatically
105: JS SDK in beta - dont document yet
106: Java SDK abandoned - dont mention
107: 
108: == CHANGELOG snippets ==
109: 
110: v2.2.0 (2024-12-15)
111: - Added webhooks
112: - Fixed: sync jobs sometimes stuck in "running"
113: - Improved: bulk insert now 3x faster
114: 
115: v2.1.0 (2024-11-01)
116: - BREAKING: Switched to JWT auth (API keys deprecated, removed in v3)
117: - Added incremental sync mode
118: - Fixed: rate limit headers missing on 429 responses
119: 
120: v2.0.0 (2024-09-15)
121: - Complete rewrite
122: - New endpoint structure
123: - Added job queue for async operations
124: 
125: == MISC ==
126: 
127: Base URL: https://api.datasync.io/v2
128: Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2 (resets daily, fake data ok)
129: 
130: Content-Type must be application/json for all POST/PUT/PATCH
131: 
132: CORS enabled for *.datasync.io domains, customers can request whitelist
133: 
134: OpenAPI spec is auto-generated but has bugs - dont use directly, needs manual cleanup

(End of file - total 134 lines)

2: """Normalize a delimited data file (CSV/TSV) whose cells may contain
3: inner-delimited multi-value fields, and report the counts needed to
