1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Normalize a delimited data file (CSV/TSV) whose cells may contain
3: inner-delimited multi-value fields, and report the counts needed to
4: reconcile a deliverable against its source.
5: 
6: Usage:
7:   python3 scripts/normalize_delimited.py <file.csv> [--delimiter ,] [--inner ;]
8:       [--fields col1,col2] [--out out.json] [--markdown] [--max-col-width 40]
9: 
10: Behavior:
11:   * Parses with the csv module (quoted fields handled correctly).
12:   * If --inner is given, every cell (or only --fields columns) that contains
13:     the inner delimiter is split into a list; a cell without it stays as-is.
14:   * Prints: row count, column list, per-column non-empty counts, per-column
15:     count of cells containing the inner delimiter, and duplicate-key check on
16:     the first column if --key is given.
17:   * With --out, writes a JSON array of row objects (inner-split values as lists).
18:   * With --markdown, prints a markdown table of the normalized rows.
19: 
20: Exit code 0 on success; row/cell counts are printed on stdout for reuse.
21: """
22: 
23: import argparse
24: import csv
25: import json
26: import sys
27: 
28: 
29: def main():
30:     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Normalize delimited data with inner multi-value cells.")
31:     ap.add_argument("path", nargs="?", default="-", help="input file, '-' for stdin")
32:     ap.add_argument("--delimiter", default=",", help="field delimiter (default ',')")
33:     ap.add_argument("--inner", default=None, help="inner delimiter for multi-value cells, e.g. ';'")
34:     ap.add_argument("--fields", default=None, help="comma-separated column names to inner-split (default: any)")
35:     ap.add_argument("--key", default=None, help="column to check for duplicate values")
36:     ap.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="write normalized rows as JSON to this path")
37:     ap.add_argument("--markdown", action="store_true", help="also print a markdown table")
38:     ap.add_argument("--max-col-width", type=int, default=40, help="markdown cell truncation width")
39:     args = ap.parse_args()
40: 
41:     handle = sys.stdin if args.path == "-" else open(args.path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig")
42:     try:
43:         reader = csv.DictReader(handle, delimiter=args.delimiter)
44:         rows = [dict(r) for r in reader]
45:         columns = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
46:     finally:
47:         if handle is not sys.stdin:
48:             handle.close()
49: 
50:     if not rows:
51:         print("ROW_COUNT 0")
52:         print("WARNING: no data rows parsed - check the delimiter")
53:         return 1
54: 
55:     split_fields = set(args.fields.split(",")) if args.fields else None
56:     inner_counts = {c: 0 for c in columns}
57:     normalized = []
58:     for row in rows:
59:         out = {}
60:         for col in columns:
61:             val = (row.get(col) or "").strip()
62:             if args.inner and val and args.inner in val and (split_fields is None or col in split_fields):
63:                 inner_counts[col] += 1
64:                 out[col] = [part.strip() for part in val.split(args.inner) if part.strip() != ""]
65:             else:
66:                 out[col] = val
67:         normalized.append(out)
68: 
69:     print("ROW_COUNT", len(normalized))
70:     print("COLUMNS", "|".join(columns))
71:     for col in columns:
72:         nonempty = sum(1 for r in normalized if r[col])
73:         print("FILLED\t%s\t%d/%d" % (col, nonempty, len(normalized)))
74:     if args.inner:
75:         for col, n in inner_counts.items():
76:             if n:
77:                 print("INNER_SPLIT\t%s\t%d" % (col, n))
78:     if args.key:
79:         if args.key not in columns:
80:             print("WARNING: key column %r not found" % args.key)
81:         else:
82:             seen, dupes = set(), []
83:             for r in normalized:
84:                 k = r[args.key]
85:                 ident = tuple(k) if isinstance(k, list) else (k,)
86:                 if ident in seen:
87:                     dupes.append(str(ident))
88:                 seen.add(ident)
89:             print("DUPLICATE_KEYS", len(dupes), "; ".join(dupes[:5]))
90: 
91:     if args.out:
92:         with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
93:             json.dump(normalized, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
94:         print("WROTE_JSON", args.out)
95: 
96:     if args.markdown:
97:         def cell(v):
98:             text = "; ".join(v) if isinstance(v, list) else str(v)
99:             text = text.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ")
100:             if len(text) > args.max_col_width:
101:                 text = text[: args.max_col_width - 1] + "\u2026"
102:             return text
103: 
104:         print("| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |")
105:         print("|" + "|".join(["---"] * len(columns)) + "|")
106:         for r in normalized:
107:             print("| " + " | ".join(cell(r[c]) for c in columns) + " |")
108:     return 0
109: 
110: 
111: if __name__ == "__main__":
112:     sys.exit(main())

The path crosses two releases — v2.1.0 (2024-11-01) and v2.2.0 (2024-12-15) — and the most impactful change on that path is the switch from API key authentication to JWT.\n\n**Companion documents:**\n\n- `API_REFERENCE.md` — full endpoint documentation for v2.2\n- `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md` — diagnostics for auth, rate limit, and webhook issues\n- `RELEASE_NOTES_v2.2.md` — what shipped in v2.2.0\n\n**Environments**\n\n| Environment | Base URL | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Production | `https://api.datasync.io/v2` | |\n| Sandbox | `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2` | Resets daily; safe for migration testing |\n\n---\n\n## 1. What changed between v2.0 and v2.2\n\n| Release | Date | Change | Impact on v2.0 integrations |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| v2.1.0 | 2024-11-01 | **JWT authentication** replaces API keys (keys deprecated; removal planned for v3) | **Action required** — plan and execute an auth migration |\n| v2.1.0 | 2024-11-01 | **Incremental sync mode** added to `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` | Optional — significant efficiency gain, easy to miss |\n| v2.1.0 | 2024-11-01 | Rate limit headers are now returned on `429` responses | Enables proper backoff handling |\n| v2.2.0 | 2024-12-15 | **Webhooks** (event subscriptions with optional HMAC signatures) | Optional — replaces polling patterns |\n| v2.2.0 | 2024-12-15 | Fixed: sync jobs occasionally stuck in `running` status | Reliability improvement |\n| v2.2.0 | 2024-12-15 | Bulk record inserts are ~3x faster | Performance improvement |\n\n**No new breaking changes were introduced in v2.2.0 itself.** The one breaking change on the v2.0 → v2.2 path is the authentication switch in v2.1. The response envelope, error codes, and all v2.0 data endpoints behave the same in v2.2.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Upgrade path overview\n\nWork through these steps in order. Each maps to a section below.\n\n1. **Test in the sandbox first.** The sandbox resets daily, so you can iterate freely against fake data.\n2. **Plan the authentication migration** (Section 3). This is the only mandatory work: legacy API keys are deprecated and will be removed in v3. Both auth methods work side by side during the deprecation window, so you can migrate in phases.\n3. **Adopt incremental sync** where you trigger syncs (Section 4). This capability shipped in v2.1 and is opt-in per request — many v2.0 integrators never noticed it.\n4. **Evaluate webhooks** for event-driven patterns (Section 5) — new in v2.2.\n5. **Revisit bulk insert batching** (Section 6) — inserts are faster in v2.2, and bulk requests draw from their own rate limit category.\n6. **Verify rate limit handling** — make sure your client reads `X-RateLimit-*` headers and backs off correctly on `429` (see `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md`).\n\n### Pre-migration checklist\n\n- [ ] Integration tested against `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2`\n- [ ] Inventory of every service/cron job/script that calls the API with a legacy API key\n- [ ] JWT login + refresh flow implemented and tested (Section 3.5–3.6)\n- [ ] Decision recorded for each service: migrate now or during the deprecation window (Section 3.4)\n- [ ] Sync calls reviewed for `mode` usage (Section 4)\n- [ ] Bulk insert chunking reviewed against the 1,000-record-per-request limit (Section 6)\n- [ ] `429` handler uses `X-RateLimit-Reset` for backoff\n- [ ] Webhook signature verification implemented if you subscribe to events (Section 5)\n\n---\n\n## 3. Authentication transition: API keys → JWT\n\n### 3.1 What changed\n\n- **v2.0** authenticated requests with a long-lived API key sent with every request.\n- **v2.1** switched to **JWT bearer tokens** obtained from `POST /auth/login`. API keys were deprecated at the same time.\n- **Deprecation window:** both methods are accepted during the transition period. API keys will be **removed in v3**.\n- The legacy key management endpoints — `GET /me/api-keys` and `POST /me/api-keys` — still operate, but they are **deprecated** and exist only to support the transition.\n\n### 3.2 What still works during the deprecation period\n\nA frequent source of confusion: *\"the key endpoints still return 200 — are my keys still valid?\"*\n\n**Yes.** During the deprecation window:\n\n- Existing API keys continue to authenticate requests.\n- `GET /me/api-keys` still lists your keys, and `POST /me/api-keys` still creates new ones (both marked deprecated in the API reference).\n- Do **not** create new API keys for new services or new deployments. New development should use JWT exclusively.\n\nThe continued operation of these endpoints is deliberate: it is what makes a phased migration possible. It is **not** a signal that API keys are a supported long-term option.\n\n### 3.3 JWT quick start\n\n```\nPOST /auth/login\n{ \"email\": \"you@example.com\", \"password\": \"...\" }\n```\n\nResponse:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": true,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"access_token\": \"eyJhbGciOi...\",\n    \"refresh_token\": \"d9f0c1...\"\n  },\n  \"meta\": { \"request_id\": \"b2c1...\", \"timestamp\": \"2024-12-15T10:00:00Z\" }\n}\n```\n\nToken facts you must design around:\n\n| Token | Lifetime | Used for |\n|---|---|---|\n| `access_token` | ~1 hour | `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` header on every API call |\n| `refresh_token` | 7 days | `POST /auth/refresh` to obtain a new access token (and new tokens) |\n\nNotes:\n\n- `POST /auth/refresh` takes the `refresh_token` in the request body — no credentials required.\n- `POST /auth/logout` invalidates tokens. If you omit the `refresh_token` in the body, **all** tokens for the user are invalidated.\n- `429` can be returned by `POST /auth/login` after too many attempts — back off and retry later.\n\n### 3.4 Decision criteria for the deprecation period\n\nBecause both methods work during the window, the right question is not *“can we defer?”* but *“which services should move first?”* Use these criteria:\n\n| Factor | Migrate now | Defer (staged) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Number of services using the key | A handful | Dozens of microservices — migrate in phases |\n| Refresh handling in your stack | Token storage/refresh already implemented | Needs infra work — start now, finish before v3 |\n| Security posture requirements | High — short-lived JWTs reduce the blast radius of leaked credentials | Low-sensitivity internal tooling can move last |\n| New services or rewrite in progress | Always JWT — never build on keys | — |\n| Creating new API keys | Stop immediately (`POST /me/api-keys` is deprecated) | — |\n| Deadline | — | **All services must be off API keys before v3**, when key support is removed |\n\n**Recommended staged approach for large fleets** (for example, an enterprise with dozens of microservices sharing one key):\n\n1. Keep the existing API key running — nothing breaks during the window.\n2. Implement a shared token service (or use your platform's secret manager) that performs login + refresh once and hands short-lived access tokens to services. This avoids 47 services each implementing refresh logic.\n3. Migrate services in waves: start with low-risk read-only consumers, finish with write-heavy services.\n4. After each wave, confirm no 401 spikes, then stop using the key in that wave's services.\n5. When the last wave is done, remove the key from all configuration — do not wait for the v3 removal date.\n\n### 3.5 Before/after: authenticating a request\n\n**Before — v2.0 pattern (API key sent with every request; header name as configured in your v2.0 integration):**\n\n```bash\ncurl -H \"X-API-Key: ak_live_xxxx\" \\\n     https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets\n```\n\n**After — v2.2 pattern (JWT bearer token):**\n\n```bash\n# 1. Exchange credentials for tokens (once per hour)\ncurl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n     -d '{\"email\":\"you@example.com\",\"password\":\"...\"}' \\\n     https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/login\n\n# 2. Call the API with the access token\ncurl -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...\" \\\n     https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets\n```\n\n### 3.6 Before/after: token lifecycle handling\n\nLong-running processes must refresh proactively or recover from expiry. A minimal Python pattern:\n\n**Before (v2.0):** static credential, no lifecycle code.\n\n```python\nAPI_KEY = \"ak_live_xxxx\"  # set once, never changes\n\ndef call(path, **kw):\n    return requests.get(f\"{BASE}/datasets\", headers={\"X-API-Key\": API_KEY})\n```\n\n**After (v2.2):** login, proactive refresh, and 401 retry.\n\n```python\nimport time, requests\n\nclass Auth:\n    def __init__(self, email, password):\n        self.email, self.password = email, password\n        self.access = self.refresh_tok = None\n        self.expires_at = 0\n\n    def token(self):\n        if time.time() > self.expires_at - 60:   # refresh 60s before expiry\n            self._login_or_refresh()\n        return self.access\n\n    def _login_or_refresh(self):\n        if self.refresh_tok:\n            r = requests.post(f\"{BASE}/auth/refresh\",\n                              json={\"refresh_token\": self.refresh_tok})\n        else:\n            r = requests.post(f\"{BASE}/auth/login\",\n                              json={\"email\": self.email, \"password\": self.password})\n        r.raise_for_status()\n        d = r.json()[\"data\"]\n        self.access, self.refresh_tok = d[\"access_token\"], d[\"refresh_token\"]\n        self.expires_at = time.time() + 55 * 60  # access tokens last ~1 hour\n\nAUTH = Auth(\"you@example.com\", \"...\")\n\ndef call(method, path, **kw):\n    headers = kw.pop(\"headers\", {})\n    headers[\"Authorization\"] = f\"Bearer {AUTH.token()}\"\n    r = requests.request(method, f\"{BASE}{path}\", headers=headers, **kw)\n    if r.status_code == 401:                 # token expired mid-flight: refresh once, retry\n        AUTH._login_or_refresh()\n        headers[\"Authorization\"] = f\"Bearer {AUTH.token()}\"\n        r = requests.request(method, f\"{BASE}{path}\", headers=headers, **kw)\n    return r\n```\n\nHandle these refresh-path responses explicitly:\n\n| Response from `POST /auth/refresh` | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| `200` | New tokens issued | Swap tokens in storage |\n| `400` | Refresh token invalid | Re-login with credentials |\n| `401` | Refresh token expired (older than 7 days) | Re-login with credentials |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Incremental sync (added in v2.1 — commonly missed)\n\n`POST /datasets/{id}/sync` existed in v2.0, so many integrators never re-read its docs. What changed in v2.1: the endpoint gained an **`incremental` mode** that transfers only what changed since the last successful sync, instead of re-syncing the entire dataset.\n\n**Key facts:**\n\n- `mode` accepts `full` or `incremental`; **the default is `full`** — you must opt in explicitly on every request.\n- The call is asynchronous: a `202` response means the job was accepted. The response body identifies the job; poll `GET /jobs/{job_id}` for `{ \"status\": \"pending\" | \"running\" | \"completed\" | \"failed\", \"progress\": 0-100, \"error\": string | null }`.\n- Sync requests draw from the dedicated **sync rate limit category**, separate from standard request limits (see `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md`).\n- v2.2 also fixed a defect where sync jobs could occasionally remain stuck in `running`.\n\n**Before — v2.0 pattern (full sync every run):**\n\n```python\nr = requests.post(f\"{BASE}/datasets/{ds_id}/sync\",\n                  headers=auth_headers,\n                  json={\"source_id\": \"src_123\", \"mode\": \"full\"})\njob_id = r.json()[\"data\"][\"job_id\"]\n```\n\n**After — v2.2 pattern (incremental, with job tracking):**\n\n```python\nr = requests.post(f\"{BASE}/datasets/{ds_id}/sync\",\n                  headers=auth_headers,\n                  json={\"source_id\": \"src_123\", \"mode\": \"incremental\"})\njob_id = r.json()[\"data\"][\"job_id\"]\n\n# Poll until the job settles\nwhile True:\n    job = requests.get(f\"{BASE}/jobs/{job_id}\", headers=auth_headers).json()[\"data\"]\n    if job[\"status\"] in (\"completed\", \"failed\"):\n        break\n    time.sleep(5)\n```\n\nWith v2.2 you can replace the polling loop entirely by subscribing to the `sync.completed` and `sync.failed` webhook events (Section 5) — poll only as a fallback.\n\n**When to use `incremental`:** any recurring or scheduled sync against a source you already synced before. Use `full` for initial loads, source reconfigurations, or after suspected drift.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Webhooks (new in v2.2)\n\nWebhooks let the API notify you when things happen, instead of you polling.\n\n### 5.1 The event list — and the one event that does *not* exist\n\n| Event | Fired when |\n|---|---|\n| `dataset.created` | A dataset is created |\n| `dataset.updated` | A dataset is updated **or archived** (see below) |\n| `sync.completed` | A sync job finishes successfully |\n| `sync.failed` | A sync job fails |\n\n> **Important — there is no `dataset.deleted` event.** `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a **soft delete**: it sets the dataset's archived flag and emits a **`dataset.updated`** event. If your webhook filter includes `dataset.deleted`, it will simply never fire. To detect archival, subscribe to `dataset.updated` and check the dataset's archived/status state in the payload. (Deleting an individual *record* via `DELETE /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` is a hard delete and is not accompanied by a dataset-level event.)\n\n### 5.2 Getting started\n\n```\nPOST /webhooks\n{ \"url\": \"https://hooks.example.com/datasync\",\n  \"events\": [\"dataset.created\", \"dataset.updated\", \"sync.completed\", \"sync.failed\"],\n  \"secret\": \"whsec_...\" }\n```\n\n- `secret` is optional but **strongly recommended**: when set, every delivery includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header containing the HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body, keyed with your secret. Verification steps and reference code are in `API_REFERENCE.md` (Webhooks → Signature verification).\n- Payload shape for every event:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"event\": \"dataset.updated\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-12-15T10:00:00Z\",\n  \"data\": { \"...\": \"event-specific fields\" }\n}\n```\n\n### 5.3 Before/after: change detection\n\n**Before (v2.0):** poll the API on a timer to notice changes.\n\n```python\nwhile True:\n    datasets = requests.get(f\"{BASE}/datasets\", headers=auth_headers).json()[\"data\"]\n    diff_against_last_snapshot(datasets)\n    time.sleep(300)\n```\n\n**After (v2.2):** react to events; poll only as a fallback.\n\n```python\n@app.post(\"/datasync\")\ndef handle(request):\n    if not signature_valid(request):          # HMAC-SHA256, see API_REFERENCE.md\n        return \"\", 400\n    body = request.get_json()\n    if body[\"event\"] == \"dataset.updated\" and body[\"data\"].get(\"archived\"):\n        handle_archival(body[\"data\"])          # replaces a \"dataset.deleted\" handler\n    elif body[\"event\"] == \"sync.completed\":\n        refresh_local_copy(body[\"data\"])\n    return \"\", 200\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Bulk record inserts\n\n`POST /datasets/{id}/records` accepts either a single record object or an array of records (**max 1,000 records per request**). In v2.2 bulk inserts are approximately **3x faster**.\n\nOne behavior change to be aware of: bulk record inserts draw from a dedicated **bulk rate limit category** with its own — lower — limits, separate from the standard request budget. On the Free tier that is **20 bulk requests per minute**. If your sync jobs post many small batches, they will hit `429` long before the standard limit is reached.\n\n**Before (v2.0):** many small requests.\n\n```python\nfor record in records:                       # N requests, N chances to be rate limited\n    requests.post(f\"{BASE}/datasets/{ds_id}/records\",\n                  headers=auth_headers, json=record)\n```\n\n**After (v2.2):** batch up to 1,000 records per request.\n\n```python\nfor chunk in chunks(records, 1000):          # ceil(N/1000) requests\n    requests.post(f\"{BASE}/datasets/{ds_id}/records\",\n                  headers=auth_headers, json=chunk)\n```\n\nBatching reduces request count (helping you stay inside the bulk rate category) *and* benefits from the v2.2 performance improvement. See `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md` for the full rate limit matrix and retry strategy.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Escalated support scenarios, resolved\n\nThe three scenarios below came through Customer Success as documentation escalations. They are reproduced here (anonymized) because each one represents a migration pattern other integrators are likely to hit.\n\n### Scenario 1 — 401 errors after upgrading, with API keys still listed in the dashboard\n\n**Symptom.** After upgrading, requests that worked in v2.0 return `401`. The legacy key management endpoints still respond successfully, which makes it look like nothing changed.\n\n**Root cause.** v2.1 switched the platform to JWT authentication. API keys are deprecated but still accepted during the transition window — so a `401` at this stage almost always means the *request* is malformed for the new auth flow (missing/misnamed header, cached expired credentials), not that the key was revoked.\n\n**Concrete solution.**\n\n1. Confirm the key still works by listing it via `GET /me/api-keys` (deprecated, but functional).\n2. Implement the JWT flow (Section 3.3 / 3.6). Exchange credentials once, store both tokens, refresh proactively before the ~1 hour access-token expiry.\n3. For large fleets, use the staged rollout in Section 3.4 — parallel auth support means API-key services keep working while JWT services come online one by one.\n4. Stop creating new API keys today; complete the switchover before v3 removes key support.\n\n**Before/after code:** Section 3.5 and 3.6.\n\n### Scenario 2 — Webhook subscribed to `dataset.deleted` never fires\n\n**Symptom.** A webhook registered for `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `dataset.deleted`, `sync.completed`, and `sync.failed` receives callbacks for everything except deletions. Datasets disappear from the active list, but no deletion event arrives.\n\n**Root cause.** `dataset.deleted` is **not an implemented event**. `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a **soft delete** (archive): the dataset's archived flag is set and a **`dataset.updated`** event is emitted. The callback *is* being sent — just under a different event name.\n\n**Concrete solution.**\n\n1. Remove `dataset.deleted` from your event subscription; it is not a valid event (valid events: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed`).\n2. Subscribe to `dataset.updated` and inspect the dataset's archived flag in the payload to distinguish archival from ordinary updates (Section 5.3).\n3. Remember the asymmetry: datasets archive (soft), individual records delete permanently (hard) — and record deletion emits no dataset-level event.\n\n### Scenario 3 — Rate limited after ~20 bulk inserts despite a 100 req/min plan limit\n\n**Symptom.** On the Free tier, standard `GET` traffic sails along at up to 100 requests/minute, but a bulk insert job starts receiving `429` after roughly 20 requests.\n\n**Root cause.** Rate limits are enforced **per category**, not just per plan. Bulk record inserts belong to the `bulk` category, which on the Free tier allows **20 requests/minute** — independent of the 100 req/min standard budget.\n\n**Concrete solution.**\n\n1. Batch up to 1,000 records per request (Section 6) — fewer, larger requests fit the bulk budget.\n2. Read `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp) from responses and pace the job accordingly; on `429`, wait until `X-RateLimit-Reset` before retrying.\n3. Design scheduled sync jobs around the per-category budgets in `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Compatibility notes and deprecations\n\n| Item | Status | Details |\n|---|---|---|\n| API key authentication | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Still functional during the transition window; removal planned for v3. Migrate to JWT. |\n| `GET /me/api-keys` | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Legacy key listing. Do not build new integrations on it. |\n| `POST /me/api-keys` | **Deprecated (v2.1)** | Legacy key creation. Do not create new keys. |\n| Response envelope | Unchanged | `{ success, data, error, meta }` since v2.0 |\n| Error semantics | Unchanged | `400` validation (with field-level `errors` array), `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `422`, `429`, `500` |\n| v2.0 data endpoints | Unchanged | All 16 operations added in v2.0 behave the same in v2.2 |\n\nNew since v2.0: 4 auth/account operations (v2.1) and 4 webhook operations (v2.2) — 24 operations in total across the API.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Quick reference: v2.0 → v2.2 cheat sheet\n\n| v2.0 pattern | v2.2 replacement |\n|---|---|\n| API key in every request header | `POST /auth/login` → `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`, refresh before ~1 h expiry |\n| Full sync on every run | `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` with `\"mode\": \"incremental\"` |\n| Polling `GET /jobs/{job_id}` in a loop | Subscribe to `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhooks (poll as fallback) |\n| Polling datasets for changes | Subscribe to `dataset.created` / `dataset.updated` |\n| Expecting a `dataset.deleted` event | Handle `dataset.updated` + archived flag (soft delete) |\n| One request per record insert | Batch arrays up to 1,000 records per `POST /datasets/{id}/records` |\n| Ignoring `429` (retry immediately) | Back off using `X-RateLimit-Reset`; respect per-category budgets |\n"}", "type": "tool_call"}]

Formatting follows the Swagger-inspired Markdown style (collapsible endpoint sections, parameter tables, response tables, cURL examples).\n\n**Base URL:** `https://api.datasync.io/v2`\n**Sandbox:** `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2` (resets daily)\n\n---\n\n## Conventions\n\n### Authentication\n\nAll endpoints require authentication unless marked *public*. Send a JWT access token in the `Authorization` header:\n\n```\nAuthorization: Bearer \n```\n\nObtain tokens via `POST /auth/login`; refresh via `POST /auth/refresh`. Access tokens live ~1 hour, refresh tokens 7 days. Legacy API key authentication is **deprecated** (removal planned for v3) — see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`.\n\n### Request format\n\n`Content-Type: application/json` is required for all `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` requests.\n\n### Response envelope\n\nEvery response is wrapped in a standard envelope:\n\n```json\n{\n \"success\": true,\n \"data\": {},\n \"error\": null,\n \"meta\": { \"request_id\": \"uuid\", \"timestamp\": \"ISO8601\" }\n}\n```\n\nOn failure, `success` is `false`, `data` is `null`, and `error` is an object: `{ \"code\": \"ERR_CODE\", \"message\": \"Human readable\", \"details\": {} }`. Validation failures (`400`) include a field-level `errors` array. Server errors (`500`) include a `request_id` in `meta` — include it when contacting support.\n\n### Error codes\n\n| HTTP code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `400` | Bad request — validation failed; body contains field-specific messages |\n| `401` | Not authenticated |\n| `403` | Forbidden — authenticated but not authorized |\n| `404` | Not found |\n| `409` | Conflict (e.g., duplicate dataset name) |\n| `422` | Unprocessable entity — business rule violation |\n| `429` | Rate limited |\n| `500` | Server error |\n\n### Rate limits\n\nRequests are counted in three categories: **standard**, **bulk**, and **sync**. Every response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp) headers; on `429`, wait until the reset time before retrying. See `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md` for the full per-tier matrix.\n\n### Pagination\n\nList endpoints accept `page` (default `1`) and `limit` (default `20`, maximum `100`).\n\n---\n\n## Endpoint inventory\n\n| # | Method | Endpoint | Rate category | Added | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `POST` | `/auth/login` | standard | v2.1.0 | active (public) |\n| 2 | `POST` | `/auth/refresh` | standard | v2.1.0 | active (public) |\n| 3 | `POST` | `/auth/logout` | standard | v2.1.0 | active |\n| 4 | `GET` | `/datasets` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 5 | `POST` | `/datasets` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 6 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 7 | `PUT` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 8 | `DELETE` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active (soft delete) |\n| 9 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}/records` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 10 | `POST` | `/datasets/{id}/records` | **bulk** | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 11 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 12 | `PATCH` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 13 | `DELETE` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active (hard delete) |\n| 14 | `POST` | `/datasets/{id}/sync` | **sync** | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 15 | `GET` | `/jobs/{job_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 16 | `GET` | `/webhooks` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 17 | `POST` | `/webhooks` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 18 | `GET` | `/webhooks/{id}` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 19 | `DELETE` | `/webhooks/{id}` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 20 | `GET` | `/me` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 21 | `PATCH` | `/me` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 22 | `GET` | `/me/api-keys` | standard | v2.0.0 | **DEPRECATED (v2.1)** |\n| 23 | `POST` | `/me/api-keys` | standard | v2.0.0 | **DEPRECATED (v2.1)** |\n| 24 | `GET` | `/me/usage` | standard | v2.1.0 | active |\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Authentication\n\n#### Authenticate and obtain tokens\n\n
\n POST /auth/login (authenticate user and get tokens — public)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------|\n> | `email` | required | string | Account email |\n> | `password` | required | string | Account password |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|--------------------------------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Tokens returned (`access_token`, `refresh_token`) |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid credentials |\n> | `429` | `application/json` | Too many attempts — back off and retry later |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -d '{\"email\":\"you@example.com\",\"password\":\"secret\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/login\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Refresh an access token\n\n
\n POST /auth/refresh (exchange a refresh token for new tokens — public)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|------------------------|\n> | `refresh_token` | required | string | Current refresh token |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|-----------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | New tokens issued |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid token |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Expired token — log in again |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -d '{\"refresh_token\":\"d9f0c1...\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/refresh\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Invalidate tokens\n\n
\n POST /auth/logout (invalidate tokens — requires auth)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|\n> | `refresh_token` | optional | string | Specific token to invalidate; if omitted, **all** tokens for the user are invalidated |\n\n*(Request body — JSON, optional)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"refresh_token\":\"d9f0c1...\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/logout\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Datasets\n\n#### List datasets\n\n
\n GET /datasets (list all datasets for the authenticated user)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------|\n> | `page` | optional | int | Page number (default `1`) |\n> | `limit` | optional | int | Items per page (default `20`, max `100`) |\n> | `status` | optional | string | Filter: `active` \\| `archived` \\| `all` (default `all`) |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|---------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset list |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> \"https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets?page=1&limit=20&status=active\"\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Create a dataset\n\n
\n POST /datasets (create a new dataset)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------|\n> | `name` | required | string | Dataset name — must be 3–100 characters and unique |\n> | `description` | optional | string | Human-readable description |\n> | `tags` | optional | array | List of tags |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `409` | `application/json` | Duplicate name |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"name\":\"Quarterly metrics\",\"description\":\"Q4 data\",\"tags\":[\"finance\"]}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets\n> ```\n\n

\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Update a dataset\n\n
\n PUT /datasets/{id} (update a dataset)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `name` | optional | string | New name (3–100 chars, unique) |\n> | `description` | optional | string | New description |\n> | `tags` | optional | array | New tag list |\n\n*(Request body — JSON; same fields as create, all optional)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X PUT -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"description\":\"Updated description\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Archive (soft-delete) a dataset\n\n

Archiving emits a **`dataset.updated`** webhook event — there is no `dataset.deleted` event.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X DELETE -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\n> ```\n\n

\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Webhooks\n\nWebhook subscriptions push notifications to your HTTPS endpoint when events occur. Supported events:\n\n| Event | Fired when |\n|---|---|\n| `dataset.created` | A dataset is created |\n| `dataset.updated` | A dataset is updated **or archived** (soft delete) |\n| `sync.completed` | A sync job completes successfully |\n| `sync.failed` | A sync job fails |\n\n> **There is no `dataset.deleted` event.** `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a soft delete (archive) that emits `dataset.updated`.\n\nPayload shape for every delivery:\n\n```json\n{\n \"event\": \"dataset.updated\",\n \"timestamp\": \"ISO8601\",\n \"data\": { \"...\" : \"event-specific fields\" }\n}\n```\n\n#### List webhooks\n\n
\n GET /webhooks (list configured webhooks)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> None\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|--------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook list |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Create a webhook\n\n
\n POST /webhooks (create a webhook subscription)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n> | `url` | required | string | HTTPS endpoint that will receive deliveries |\n> | `events` | required | array | Events to subscribe to: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed` |\n> | `secret` | optional | string | Signing secret — when set, deliveries include an `X-Webhook-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body) |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"url\":\"https://hooks.example.com/datasync\",\"events\":[\"dataset.created\",\"dataset.updated\",\"sync.completed\",\"sync.failed\"],\"secret\":\"whsec_...\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Get webhook details\n\n
\n GET /webhooks/{id} (get webhook details)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------|-----------|-----------|-------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Webhook ID |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks/wh_001\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Delete a webhook\n\n
\n DELETE /webhooks/{id} (remove a webhook subscription)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------|-----------|-----------|-------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Webhook ID |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X DELETE -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks/wh_001\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n### Webhook signature verification\n\nWhen a webhook is created **with a `secret`**, every delivery includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header containing the **HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body**, keyed with that secret. Verify it before processing any delivery:\n\n1. **Read the raw request body** — the exact bytes as received. Do *not* re-serialize a parsed JSON object; key ordering and whitespace differences will change the signature.\n2. **Compute the expected signature** — HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body using your webhook secret as the key.\n3. **Compare in constant time** — use a timing-safe comparison (e.g., `hmac.compare_digest` in Python). Never compare with `==`.\n4. **Reject mismatches** — return an error status (e.g., `400`) and do not process the payload.\n\nReference implementation (Python):\n\n```python\nimport hmac, hashlib\n\ndef verify_webhook(request_body: bytes, received_signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:\n expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), request_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()\n return hmac.compare_digest(expected, received_signature)\n\n# In your handler:\n# sig = request.headers.get(\"X-Webhook-Signature\")\n# if not verify_webhook(request.get_data(), sig, WEBHOOK_SECRET):\n# abort(400)\n```\n\nCommon verification failures:\n\n| Symptom | Cause |\n|---|---|\n| Every signature check fails | Verifying against the parsed/re-serialized JSON instead of the raw body |\n| Signature valid locally, missing at the receiver | A proxy or framework consumed the body before your handler read the raw bytes |\n| Intermittent failures after rotation | An old webhook (old secret) still active alongside the new one — delete the stale subscription |\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Account\n\n#### Get current user profile\n\n
\n GET /me (get the current user profile)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> None\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|-------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | User profile |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/me\n> ```\n\n

Before you start: collect diagnostics\n\nEvery API response includes a `meta` object:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"success\": false,\n  \"data\": null,\n  \"error\": { \"code\": \"ERR_CODE\", \"message\": \"Human readable\", \"details\": {} },\n  \"meta\": { \"request_id\": \"b2c1...\", \"timestamp\": \"2024-12-15T10:00:00Z\" }\n}\n```\n\n- Always capture **`meta.request_id`** — support uses it to locate the exact request in server logs.\n- `400` validation failures include an `errors` array with field-specific messages — read it before guessing.\n- `500` responses are logged server-side; retry with backoff and provide the `request_id` if the problem persists.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Authentication error diagnostics\n\n### 1.1 `401 Unauthorized` — decision tree\n\nWork down the list in order:\n\n1. **Is the `Authorization` header present and well-formed?**\n   Correct format: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.\n   - Missing header → `401`.\n   - Wrong scheme (e.g., sending the token without the `Bearer` prefix, or a legacy API key credential in a bearer-style header) → `401`. This is the single most common cause of 401s reported after upgrading from v2.0.\n2. **Has the access token expired?** Access tokens live **~1 hour**. If your process caches a token across long runs, refresh it (`POST /auth/refresh`) proactively — don't wait for the 401.\n3. **Was the token invalidated?** `POST /auth/logout` invalidates tokens — and if called **without** a `refresh_token` in the body, it invalidates **all** tokens for the user. If another team member or job ran a full logout, every outstanding token stops working. Re-login.\n4. **Is the refresh token the problem?** Distinguish the two refresh failures:\n   - `400` from `POST /auth/refresh` → the refresh token is **invalid** — re-login with credentials.\n   - `401` from `POST /auth/refresh` → the refresh token has **expired** (they last **7 days**) — re-login with credentials.\n5. **Still authenticating with a legacy API key?** Keys remain functional during the deprecation window (removal planned for v3), but they are deprecated. If a request with a key returns 401, verify the key is still listed via `GET /me/api-keys` and that your client is sending the credential exactly as configured in your v2.0 integration. Plan the JWT migration regardless — see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`.\n\n### 1.2 `401` vs `403` — which one means what\n\n| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| `401` | Not authenticated — the server cannot verify who you are | Fix the token (sections 1.1) |\n| `403` | Forbidden — authenticated, but not authorized for this resource | Use credentials/resource your user actually owns |\n\n**Known behavior:** in some cases an authorization failure (valid token, insufficient permissions) is reported as `401` instead of `403`. If your token decodes as valid and unexpired but you still receive `401` on a resource you expect to access, treat it as a potential permissions issue: verify ownership of the resource, and if the problem persists, contact support with the `request_id` from `meta`.\n\n### 1.3 Throttling on the login endpoint\n\n`POST /auth/login` can return `429` (too many attempts) independently of other rate limits. Back off and retry later; do not loop login attempts in a retry storm. Batch services behind a shared token service so 40+ processes are not each performing logins.\n\n### 1.4 Auth error quick reference\n\n| Where | Response | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Any endpoint | `401` | Not authenticated / token expired / token invalidated | Check header, refresh or re-login |\n| Any endpoint | `403` | Authenticated but not authorized | Check resource ownership/permissions |\n| `POST /auth/login` | `400` | Invalid credentials | Check email/password |\n| `POST /auth/login` | `429` | Too many attempts | Back off; centralize token acquisition |\n| `POST /auth/refresh` | `400` | Invalid refresh token | Re-login |\n| `POST /auth/refresh` | `401` | Refresh token expired (7 days) | Re-login |\n\n---\n\n## 2. Rate limiting\n\n### 2.1 Categories — the part most integrations miss\n\nRate limits are enforced **per category**, not only per plan. Every endpoint belongs to exactly one category:\n\n| Category | Endpoints counted | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `standard` | All endpoints **except** the two below (22 of 24 operations) | The default budget |\n| `bulk` | `POST /datasets/{id}/records` only | Separate budget, **lower** than standard |\n| `sync` | `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` only | Separate budget, independent of standard |\n\nSo on the Free tier, 60 standard `GET` requests plus 25 bulk inserts in the same minute does **not** fit: the 60 are fine, the 25 bulk requests exceed the 20/min bulk budget and the 21st onward get `429` — even though you are far under 100 req/min overall.\n\n### 2.2 Limits by tier\n\n| Tier | Standard | Bulk | Sync | Daily cap |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Free | 100 req/min | **20 req/min** | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | 10,000 req/day |\n| Pro | 1,000 req/min | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | None |\n| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom |\n\nThe authoritative limit for your plan and category is always exposed in the `X-RateLimit-Limit` response header — read it once from a live call rather than hardcoding assumptions.\n\n### 2.3 Rate limit response headers\n\nEvery response (success or `429`) carries:\n\n| Header | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Maximum requests per window for that category |\n| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests remaining in the current window |\n| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp when the window resets |\n\n> Headers on `429` responses have been reliable since v2.1 (a v2.0 defect omitted them). If you built retry logic against v2.0 that couldn't see headers on 429s, it will work correctly now.\n\n### 2.4 `429` handling and retry strategy\n\n1. **Stop, don't hammer.** On `429`, wait until `X-RateLimit-Reset` before retrying — do not retry in a tight loop, which only prolongs the lockout.\n2. **Use `X-RateLimit-Remaining` proactively.** Throttle or defer work when remaining budget approaches zero, instead of reacting to 429s.\n3. **Batch bulk work.** `POST /datasets/{id}/records` accepts up to **1,000 records per request** — one large request consumes one bulk-budget slot and moves 50x the data of 50 small ones.\n4. **Separate your workers.** Standard traffic and bulk/sync traffic draw from different budgets; schedule them on independent schedules so a sync job cannot starve interactive traffic.\n5. **Space sync triggers.** Sync requests have their own category; trigger dataset syncs sequentially or on a jittered schedule rather than firing many at once.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Webhook issues\n\n### 3.1 Not receiving callbacks — checklist\n\n1. **List your actual subscriptions** with `GET /webhooks` and compare the `events` array to what you expect.\n2. **Are you subscribed to an event that doesn't exist?** The valid events are exactly: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed`. There is **no `dataset.deleted` event** — a subscription entry for it never fires.\n3. **Looking for deletion notifications?** `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a **soft delete** (archive): the dataset's archived flag is set and a **`dataset.updated`** event is delivered. Detect archival by inspecting the archived/status state in the `dataset.updated` payload. (Record-level `DELETE /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` is a hard delete; it does not emit a dataset-level event.)\n4. **Waiting for job results?** Sync jobs emit `sync.completed` / `sync.failed`; you can replace `GET /jobs/{job_id}` polling with these events.\n5. **Is your receiver reachable?** Confirm the `url` registered on the webhook is publicly reachable via HTTPS.\n\n### 3.2 Signature verification failures\n\nWhen a webhook is created with a `secret`, deliveries carry `X-Webhook-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body). If verification fails:\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Every delivery fails verification | Signature computed over re-serialized JSON instead of the **raw body bytes** | Hash the raw body exactly as received |\n| Fails only behind a proxy/framework | Body was consumed/re-encoded before your handler | Access the raw request body in your handler |\n| Fails on some webhooks only | Multiple subscriptions with different/rotated secrets | Confirm you use the secret that belongs to each webhook; delete stale subscriptions |\n| Works locally, fails in production | Secret mismatch between environments | Keep per-environment secrets in your secret store |\n\nFull verification steps and reference code: `API_REFERENCE.md` → Webhooks → *Webhook signature verification*.\n\n### 3.3 Payload shape\n\nEvery delivery uses the same envelope — parse defensively and route on the `event` field:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"event\": \"dataset.updated\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"ISO8601\",\n  \"data\": { \"...\" : \"event-specific fields\" }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Common migration pitfalls (v2.0 → v2.2)\n\nCompiled from recurring support patterns. Each row states the mistake, the observable symptom, and the correct behavior.\n\n| # | Pitfall | Symptom | Correct behavior |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Assuming old auth still works unchanged | `401` after upgrade | JWT is the standard since v2.1; API keys are deprecated but still work during the window — verify header format first (`MIGRATION_GUIDE` §3) |\n| 2 | Caching access tokens beyond their ~1 h lifetime | Sudden `401`s after an hour of operation | Refresh proactively or retry once on 401 after refreshing |\n| 3 | Subscribing to `dataset.deleted` | No callbacks when datasets are archived | Event doesn't exist; `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a soft delete that emits `dataset.updated` |\n| 4 | Treating dataset deletion as permanent | Dataset \"gone\" but still in storage | Soft delete sets the archived flag; retrieve with `GET /datasets?status=archived`. Record deletion (`.../records/{record_id}`) **is** a hard delete |\n| 5 | Hammering bulk inserts | `429` after ~20 requests on Free tier | Bulk is its own rate category (20 req/min on Free); batch up to 1,000 records per request |\n| 6 | Assuming one global rate limit | Unexpected `429` while \"well under the limit\" | Limits are per category: standard / bulk / sync |\n| 7 | Requesting `limit` > 100 on list endpoints | Truncated results or validation error | `limit` defaults to 20, **max 100**; page through with `page` |\n| 8 | Invalid dataset names | `400` on create | Name must be 3–100 characters |\n| 9 | Duplicate dataset names | `409` on create | Names must be unique — catch 409 and reuse/update the existing dataset |\n| 10 | Missing `Content-Type: application/json` | `400` on POST/PUT/PATCH | The header is required for all body-sending requests |\n| 11 | Sending `filter` as an unencoded object | Filter ignored or `400` | The `filter` parameter is **JSON-encoded** (URL-encode it in query strings) |\n| 12 | Assuming `sort` descends by default | \"Wrong\" ordering | `order` defaults to `asc` — set `order=desc` explicitly |\n| 13 | Running syncs in `full` mode out of habit | Slow, heavy sync jobs | `mode` defaults to `full`; pass `incremental` for recurring syncs (v2.1 feature) |\n| 14 | Treating the `202` from `/sync` as completion | Missing data; no job tracking | `202` = job accepted. Track via `GET /jobs/{job_id}` or `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhooks |\n| 15 | Missing rate limit headers on 429s (v2.0 behavior) | Retry logic without backoff timing | Fixed in v2.1 — headers are present on all responses, including `429` |\n| 16 | Ignoring `422` | Confusing business-rule failures with validation bugs | `400` = field validation (see `errors` array); `422` = business rule violation |\n| 17 | Retrying `500` immediately and repeatedly | Extended disruption | Back off; include `meta.request_id` in the support ticket |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Escalated scenario walkthroughs\n\nThe three Customer Success escalations that triggered this documentation, anonymized, with the resolution paths.\n\n### Scenario A — \"JWT migration breaking our integration\" (Enterprise, dozens of microservices)\n\n- **Symptom:** `401` errors after upgrading; API keys still visible in the dashboard; legacy key endpoints still return 200; no published transition guidance.\n- **Diagnosis:** v2.1 switched to JWT and deprecated API keys. Keys remain valid during the deprecation window (removal in v3), and parallel authentication is supported — so a working integration can move service by service.\n- **Resolution:** staged migration — keep keys for un-migrated services, stand up a shared token service for JWT issuance/refresh, migrate waves of services, retire the key when the last wave completes. Decision criteria and before/after code: `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md` §3.\n- **Prevention:** never create new API keys; treat `GET`/`POST /me/api-keys` as transition-only.\n\n### Scenario B — \"Webhook not firing for deleted datasets\" (Pro tier)\n\n- **Symptom:** webhook subscribed to five event names; callbacks received for `created`/`updated` but never for `dataset.deleted`.\n- **Diagnosis:** `dataset.deleted` is not an implemented event. `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a soft delete (archive) that triggers `dataset.updated`.\n- **Resolution:** remove `dataset.deleted` from the subscription; subscribe to `dataset.updated` and branch on the archived flag in the payload (`MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md` §5.3). Valid events: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed`.\n- **Prevention:** validate event names against the table in §3.1 when configuring webhooks.\n\n### Scenario C — \"Rate limiting inconsistent between endpoints\" (Free tier)\n\n- **Symptom:** ~20 bulk inserts trigger `429` while standard GET traffic at 100 req/min works fine; docs appeared to promise a single 100 req/min limit.\n- **Diagnosis:** limits are enforced per category. Bulk inserts belong to the `bulk` category (20 req/min on Free), independent of the standard budget.\n- **Resolution:** batch up to 1,000 records per request, read `X-RateLimit-Remaining`/`X-RateLimit-Reset` and pace jobs accordingly (`MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md` §6; §2 of this guide).\n- **Prevention:** design sync/insert jobs against the per-category matrix in §2.2, not the single-plan number.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Error code reference\n\n| HTTP code | Meaning | What to do |\n|---|---|---|\n| `400` | Bad request — validation failed | Read the field-level `errors` array in the body; fix the payload. (On `/auth/refresh`: invalid refresh token → re-login) |\n| `401` | Not authenticated | Follow the decision tree in §1.1 |\n| `403` | Forbidden — authenticated but not authorized | Check resource ownership/permissions |\n| `404` | Not found — including resources owned by another user | Verify the ID; note `404` is also returned for datasets you don't own |\n| `409` | Conflict | E.g., duplicate dataset name — reuse or rename |\n| `422` | Unprocessable entity — business rule violation | The request is syntactically valid but violates a rule; adjust the operation |\n| `429` | Rate limited | Wait until `X-RateLimit-Reset`; check which category you exhausted (§2) |\n| `500` | Server error | Retry with backoff; if persistent, contact support with `meta.request_id` |\n"}", "type": "tool_call"}]

1: # Developer Notes - DataSync API
2: # These are internal notes from the dev team - NOT for external publication
3: # Last updated by multiple contributors
4: 
5: == AUTH STUFF ==
6: We use JWT tokens now. Changed from API keys last sprint (v2.1).
7: Token expires in 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
8: Header format: Authorization: Bearer <token>
9: Login endpoint: POST /auth/login - takes email+password, returns tokens
10: Refresh: POST /auth/refresh - takes refresh_token in body
11: 
12: BUG: Sometimes 401 returns instead of 403 when token valid but perms wrong
13: TODO: Fix in next sprint (JIRA-4521)
14: 
15: == DATA ENDPOINTS ==
16: 
17: /datasets - GET list all datasets for user
18: params: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100), status (active|archived|all)
19: returns array of dataset objects
20: 
21: /datasets/{id} - GET single dataset
22: 404 if not found or not owned by user
23: 
24: /datasets - POST create new dataset
25: body: { name: string (required, 3-100 chars), description: string (optional), tags: array }
26: returns created dataset with id
27: 
28: /datasets/{id} - PUT update dataset
29: same body as POST but all fields optional
30: returns updated dataset
31: 
32: /datasets/{id} - DELETE soft delete (sets archived flag)
33: returns 204 no content
34: 
35: /datasets/{id}/records - GET records in dataset
36: pagination same as /datasets list
37: params: sort (field name), order (asc|desc), filter (JSON encoded query)
38: 
39: /datasets/{id}/records - POST add record(s)
40: body can be single object or array for bulk insert
41: max 1000 records per request
42: 
43: /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} - PATCH update single record
44: body: partial record object
45: 
46: /datasets/{id}/sync - POST trigger sync with external source
47: body: { source_id: string, mode: "full"|"incremental" }
48: returns job_id for async tracking
49: 
50: /jobs/{job_id} - GET check job status
51: response: { status: "pending"|"running"|"completed"|"failed", progress: 0-100, error: string|null }
52: 
53: == ERROR CODES ==
54: 
55: 400 - bad request (validation failed) - body has "errors" array with field-specific messages
56: 401 - not authenticated
57: 403 - forbidden (authenticated but not authorized)
58: 404 - not found
59: 409 - conflict (e.g., duplicate name)
60: 422 - unprocessable entity (business rule violation)
61: 429 - rate limited (100 req/min for free tier, 1000 for pro)
62: 500 - server error (we log these, include request_id in response for support)
63: 
64: == RESPONSE FORMAT ==
65: 
66: All responses wrapped:
67: {
68:   "success": true|false,
69:   "data": <payload>|null,
70:   "error": null|{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} },
71:   "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" }
72: }
73: 
74: == WEBHOOKS (v2.2 feature) ==
75: 
76: POST /webhooks - create webhook
77: body: { url: string, events: ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"], secret: string (optional, for HMAC signing) }
78: 
79: GET /webhooks - list webhooks
80: DELETE /webhooks/{id} - remove webhook
81: 
82: Webhook payload:
83: {
84:   "event": "event.type",
85:   "timestamp": "ISO8601",
86:   "data": { <event specific> }
87: }
88: 
89: If secret provided, we send X-Webhook-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 of body
90: 
91: == RATE LIMITS ==
92: 
93: Free tier: 100 requests/minute, 10000/day
94: Pro tier: 1000 requests/minute, unlimited daily
95: Enterprise: custom
96: 
97: Headers returned:
98: X-RateLimit-Limit: <max>
99: X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining>
100: X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix timestamp>
101: 
102: == SDK notes ==
103: 
104: Python SDK wraps all this, handles auth refresh automatically
105: JS SDK in beta - dont document yet
106: Java SDK abandoned - dont mention
107: 
108: == CHANGELOG snippets ==
109: 
110: v2.2.0 (2024-12-15)
111: - Added webhooks
112: - Fixed: sync jobs sometimes stuck in "running"
113: - Improved: bulk insert now 3x faster
114: 
115: v2.1.0 (2024-11-01)
116: - BREAKING: Switched to JWT auth (API keys deprecated, removed in v3)
117: - Added incremental sync mode
118: - Fixed: rate limit headers missing on 429 responses
119: 
120: v2.0.0 (2024-09-15)
121: - Complete rewrite
122: - New endpoint structure
123: - Added job queue for async operations
124: 
125: == MISC ==
126: 
127: Base URL: https://api.datasync.io/v2
128: Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2 (resets daily, fake data ok)
129: 
130: Content-Type must be application/json for all POST/PUT/PATCH
131: 
132: CORS enabled for *.datasync.io domains, customers can request whitelist
133: 
134: OpenAPI spec is auto-generated but has bugs - dont use directly, needs manual cleanup

(End of file - total 134 lines)

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Normalize a delimited data file (CSV/TSV) whose cells may contain
3: inner-delimited multi-value fields, and report the counts needed to
4: reconcile a deliverable against its source.
5: 
6: Usage:
7:   python3 scripts/normalize_delimited.py <file.csv> [--delimiter ,] [--inner ;]
8:       [--fields col1,col2] [--out out.json] [--markdown] [--max-col-width 40]
9: 
10: Behavior:
11:   * Parses with the csv module (quoted fields handled correctly).
12:   * If --inner is given, every cell (or only --fields columns) that contains
13:     the inner delimiter is split into a list; a cell without it stays as-is.
14:   * Prints: row count, column list, per-column non-empty counts, per-column
15:     count of cells containing the inner delimiter, and duplicate-key check on
16:     the first column if --key is given.
17:   * With --out, writes a JSON array of row objects (inner-split values as lists).
18:   * With --markdown, prints a markdown table of the normalized rows.
19: 
20: Exit code 0 on success; row/cell counts are printed on stdout for reuse.
21: """
22: 
23: import argparse
24: import csv
25: import json
26: import sys
27: 
28: 
29: def main():
30:     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Normalize delimited data with inner multi-value cells.")
31:     ap.add_argument("path", nargs="?", default="-", help="input file, '-' for stdin")
32:     ap.add_argument("--delimiter", default=",", help="field delimiter (default ',')")
33:     ap.add_argument("--inner", default=None, help="inner delimiter for multi-value cells, e.g. ';'")
34:     ap.add_argument("--fields", default=None, help="comma-separated column names to inner-split (default: any)")
35:     ap.add_argument("--key", default=None, help="column to check for duplicate values")
36:     ap.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="write normalized rows as JSON to this path")
37:     ap.add_argument("--markdown", action="store_true", help="also print a markdown table")
38:     ap.add_argument("--max-col-width", type=int, default=40, help="markdown cell truncation width")
39:     args = ap.parse_args()
40: 
41:     handle = sys.stdin if args.path == "-" else open(args.path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig")
42:     try:
43:         reader = csv.DictReader(handle, delimiter=args.delimiter)
44:         rows = [dict(r) for r in reader]
45:         columns = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
46:     finally:
47:         if handle is not sys.stdin:
48:             handle.close()
49: 
50:     if not rows:
51:         print("ROW_COUNT 0")
52:         print("WARNING: no data rows parsed - check the delimiter")
53:         return 1
54: 
55:     split_fields = set(args.fields.split(",")) if args.fields else None
56:     inner_counts = {c: 0 for c in columns}
57:     normalized = []
58:     for row in rows:
59:         out = {}
60:         for col in columns:
61:             val = (row.get(col) or "").strip()
62:             if args.inner and val and args.inner in val and (split_fields is None or col in split_fields):
63:                 inner_counts[col] += 1
64:                 out[col] = [part.strip() for part in val.split(args.inner) if part.strip() != ""]
65:             else:
66:                 out[col] = val
67:         normalized.append(out)
68: 
69:     print("ROW_COUNT", len(normalized))
70:     print("COLUMNS", "|".join(columns))
71:     for col in columns:
72:         nonempty = sum(1 for r in normalized if r[col])
73:         print("FILLED\t%s\t%d/%d" % (col, nonempty, len(normalized)))
74:     if args.inner:
75:         for col, n in inner_counts.items():
76:             if n:
77:                 print("INNER_SPLIT\t%s\t%d" % (col, n))
78:     if args.key:
79:         if args.key not in columns:
80:             print("WARNING: key column %r not found" % args.key)
81:         else:
82:             seen, dupes = set(), []
83:             for r in normalized:
84:                 k = r[args.key]
85:                 ident = tuple(k) if isinstance(k, list) else (k,)
86:                 if ident in seen:
87:                     dupes.append(str(ident))
88:                 seen.add(ident)
89:             print("DUPLICATE_KEYS", len(dupes), "; ".join(dupes[:5]))
90: 
91:     if args.out:
92:         with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
93:             json.dump(normalized, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
94:         print("WROTE_JSON", args.out)
95: 
96:     if args.markdown:
97:         def cell(v):
98:             text = "; ".join(v) if isinstance(v, list) else str(v)
99:             text = text.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ")
100:             if len(text) > args.max_col_width:
101:                 text = text[: args.max_col_width - 1] + "\u2026"
102:             return text
103: 
104:         print("| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |")
105:         print("|" + "|".join(["---"] * len(columns)) + "|")
106:         for r in normalized:
107:             print("| " + " | ".join(cell(r[c]) for c in columns) + " |")
108:     return 0
109: 
110: 
111: if __name__ == "__main__":
112:     sys.exit(main())

- Async: 202 + job_id; poll GET /jobs/{job_id} (status/progress/error), or subscribe to sync.completed / sync.failed webhooks (v2.2) instead of polling.

Authentication error diagnostics\n\n### 1.1 `401 Unauthorized` — decision tree\n\nWork down the list in order:\n\n1. **Is the `Authorization` header present and well-formed?**\n   Correct format: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.\n   - Missing header → `401`.\n   - Wrong scheme (e.g., sending the token without the `Bearer` prefix, or a legacy API key credential in a bearer-style header) → `401`. This is the single most common cause of 401s reported after upgrading from v2.0.\n2. **Has the access token expired?** Access tokens live **~1 hour**. If your process caches a token across long runs, refresh it (`POST /auth/refresh`) proactively — don't wait for the 401.\n3. **Was the token invalidated?** `POST /auth/logout` invalidates tokens — and if called **without** a `refresh_token` in the body, it invalidates **all** tokens for the user. If another team member or job ran a full logout, every outstanding token stops working. Re-login.\n4. **Is the refresh token the problem?** Distinguish the two refresh failures:\n   - `400` from `POST /auth/refresh` → the refresh token is **invalid** — re-login with credentials.\n   - `401` from `POST /auth/refresh` → the refresh token has **expired** (they last **7 days**) — re-login with credentials.\n5. **Still authenticating with a legacy API key?** Keys remain functional during the deprecation window (removal planned for v3), but they are deprecated. {"content": "# Release Notes — DataSync API v2.2.0

## [2.2.0] (2024-12-15)

> DataSync API v2.2 introduces webhooks for event-driven integrations, resolves a sync-job reliability defect, and delivers a major bulk-insert performance improvement. No breaking changes and no required upgrade actions — the release is a drop-in update for existing v2.0/v2.1 integrations.

### Upgrade Steps

* No action required — existing integrations continue to work against v2.2 without changes.
* Recommended (optional):
  * Subscribe to webhooks (`POST /webhooks`) to replace polling patterns; provide a `secret` at creation time and verify the `X-Webhook-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body) on every delivery. See `API_REFERENCE.md` → Webhooks.
  * Review bulk record inserts: `POST /datasets/{id}/records` accepts up to 1,000 records per request and is now ~3x faster — batching pays off double (see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md` §6).
  * If you trigger dataset syncs, prefer `"mode": "incremental"` for recurring jobs (introduced in v2.1) and confirm your job-polling or `sync.completed`/`sync.failed` handling works with the fixed job lifecycle.

### Breaking Changes

* None in v2.2.0.
* Reminder — ongoing deprecation from v2.1: API key authentication is deprecated and will be removed in v3. JWT authentication (`POST /auth/login`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`) is the supported method. API keys and the legacy `GET`/`POST /me/api-keys` endpoints remain functional during the deprecation window. New integrations must not use API keys. Migration guidance: `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md` §3.

### New Features

* **Webhooks** — subscribe an HTTPS endpoint to platform events instead of polling:
  * Endpoints: `GET /webhooks`, `POST /webhooks`, `GET /webhooks/{id}`, `DELETE /webhooks/{id}`.
  * Supported events: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed`.
  * Note: there is no `dataset.deleted` event — `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a soft delete (archive) that emits `dataset.updated`. Detect archival via the dataset's archived flag in the `dataset.updated` payload.
  * Optional signing secret: deliveries include an `X-Webhook-Signature` header with the HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body for verification.
  * Full documentation, including signature verification steps and reference code: `API_REFERENCE.md` → Webhooks.

### Bug Fixes

* **Sync jobs occasionally stuck in `running`** — async sync jobs no longer remain in the `running` state indefinitely; `GET /jobs/{job_id}` now reliably transitions to `completed` or `failed`.

### Performance Improvements

* **Bulk record inserts are ~3x faster.** `POST /datasets/{id}/records` (single object or array, max 1,000 records per request) processes large batches roughly three times faster than in v2.1.

### Other Changes

* None.

1: # Developer Notes - DataSync API
2: # These are internal notes from the dev team - NOT for external publication
3: # Last updated by multiple contributors
4: 
5: == AUTH STUFF ==
6: We use JWT tokens now. Changed from API keys last sprint (v2.1).
7: Token expires in 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
8: Header format: Authorization: Bearer <token>
9: Login endpoint: POST /auth/login - takes email+password, returns tokens
10: Refresh: POST /auth/refresh - takes refresh_token in body
11: 
12: BUG: Sometimes 401 returns instead of 403 when token valid but perms wrong
13: TODO: Fix in next sprint (JIRA-4521)
14: 
15: == DATA ENDPOINTS ==
16: 
17: /datasets - GET list all datasets for user
18: params: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100), status (active|archived|all)
19: returns array of dataset objects
20: 
21: /datasets/{id} - GET single dataset
22: 404 if not found or not owned by user
23: 
24: /datasets - POST create new dataset
25: body: { name: string (required, 3-100 chars), description: string (optional), tags: array }
26: returns created dataset with id
27: 
28: /datasets/{id} - PUT update dataset
29: same body as POST but all fields optional
30: returns updated dataset
31: 
32: /datasets/{id} - DELETE soft delete (sets archived flag)
33: returns 204 no content
34: 
35: /datasets/{id}/records - GET records in dataset
36: pagination same as /datasets list
37: params: sort (field name), order (asc|desc), filter (JSON encoded query)
38: 
39: /datasets/{id}/records - POST add record(s)
40: body can be single object or array for bulk insert
41: max 1000 records per request
42: 
43: /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} - PATCH update single record
44: body: partial record object
45: 
46: /datasets/{id}/sync - POST trigger sync with external source
47: body: { source_id: string, mode: "full"|"incremental" }
48: returns job_id for async tracking
49: 
50: /jobs/{job_id} - GET check job status
51: response: { status: "pending"|"running"|"completed"|"failed", progress: 0-100, error: string|null }
52: 
53: == ERROR CODES ==
54: 
55: 400 - bad request (validation failed) - body has "errors" array with field-specific messages
56: 401 - not authenticated
57: 403 - forbidden (authenticated but not authorized)
58: 404 - not found
59: 409 - conflict (e.g., duplicate name)
60: 422 - unprocessable entity (business rule violation)
61: 429 - rate limited (100 req/min for free tier, 1000 for pro)
62: 500 - server error (we log these, include request_id in response for support)
63: 
64: == RESPONSE FORMAT ==
65: 
66: All responses wrapped:
67: {
68:   "success": true|false,
69:   "data": <payload>|null,
70:   "error": null|{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} },
71:   "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" }
72: }
73: 
74: == WEBHOOKS (v2.2 feature) ==
75: 
76: POST /webhooks - create webhook
77: body: { url: string, events: ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"], secret: string (optional, for HMAC signing) }
78: 
79: GET /webhooks - list webhooks
80: DELETE /webhooks/{id} - remove webhook
81: 
82: Webhook payload:
83: {
84:   "event": "event.type",
85:   "timestamp": "ISO8601",
86:   "data": { <event specific> }
87: }
88: 
89: If secret provided, we send X-Webhook-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 of body
90: 
91: == RATE LIMITS ==
92: 
93: Free tier: 100 requests/minute, 10000/day
94: Pro tier: 1000 requests/minute, unlimited daily
95: Enterprise: custom
96: 
97: Headers returned:
98: X-RateLimit-Limit: <max>
99: X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining>
100: X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix timestamp>
101: 
102: == SDK notes ==
103: 
104: Python SDK wraps all this, handles auth refresh automatically
105: JS SDK in beta - dont document yet
106: Java SDK abandoned - dont mention
107: 
108: == CHANGELOG snippets ==
109: 
110: v2.2.0 (2024-12-15)
111: - Added webhooks
112: - Fixed: sync jobs sometimes stuck in "running"
113: - Improved: bulk insert now 3x faster
114: 
115: v2.1.0 (2024-11-01)
116: - BREAKING: Switched to JWT auth (API keys deprecated, removed in v3)
117: - Added incremental sync mode
118: - Fixed: rate limit headers missing on 429 responses
119: 
120: v2.0.0 (2024-09-15)
121: - Complete rewrite
122: - New endpoint structure
123: - Added job queue for async operations
124: 
125: == MISC ==
126: 
127: Base URL: https://api.datasync.io/v2
128: Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2 (resets daily, fake data ok)
129: 
130: Content-Type must be application/json for all POST/PUT/PATCH
131: 
132: CORS enabled for *.datasync.io domains, customers can request whitelist
133: 
134: OpenAPI spec is auto-generated but has bugs - dont use directly, needs manual cleanup

(End of file - total 134 lines)
</content>", "type": "text"}]
