Formatting follows the Swagger-inspired Markdown style (collapsible endpoint sections, parameter tables, response tables, cURL examples).\n\n**Base URL:** `https://api.datasync.io/v2`\n**Sandbox:** `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2` (resets daily)\n\n---\n\n## Conventions\n\n### Authentication\n\nAll endpoints require authentication unless marked *public*. Send a JWT access token in the `Authorization` header:\n\n```\nAuthorization: Bearer \n```\n\nObtain tokens via `POST /auth/login`; refresh via `POST /auth/refresh`. Access tokens live ~1 hour, refresh tokens 7 days. Legacy API key authentication is **deprecated** (removal planned for v3) — see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`.\n\n### Request format\n\n`Content-Type: application/json` is required for all `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` requests.\n\n### Response envelope\n\nEvery response is wrapped in a standard envelope:\n\n```json\n{\n \"success\": true,\n \"data\": {},\n \"error\": null,\n \"meta\": { \"request_id\": \"uuid\", \"timestamp\": \"ISO8601\" }\n}\n```\n\nOn failure, `success` is `false`, `data` is `null`, and `error` is an object: `{ \"code\": \"ERR_CODE\", \"message\": \"Human readable\", \"details\": {} }`. Validation failures (`400`) include a field-level `errors` array. Server errors (`500`) include a `request_id` in `meta` — include it when contacting support.\n\n### Error codes\n\n| HTTP code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `400` | Bad request — validation failed; body contains field-specific messages |\n| `401` | Not authenticated |\n| `403` | Forbidden — authenticated but not authorized |\n| `404` | Not found |\n| `409` | Conflict (e.g., duplicate dataset name) |\n| `422` | Unprocessable entity — business rule violation |\n| `429` | Rate limited |\n| `500` | Server error |\n\n### Rate limits\n\nRequests are counted in three categories: **standard**, **bulk**, and **sync**. Every response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp) headers; on `429`, wait until the reset time before retrying. See `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md` for the full per-tier matrix.\n\n### Pagination\n\nList endpoints accept `page` (default `1`) and `limit` (default `20`, maximum `100`).\n\n---\n\n## Endpoint inventory\n\n| # | Method | Endpoint | Rate category | Added | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `POST` | `/auth/login` | standard | v2.1.0 | active (public) |\n| 2 | `POST` | `/auth/refresh` | standard | v2.1.0 | active (public) |\n| 3 | `POST` | `/auth/logout` | standard | v2.1.0 | active |\n| 4 | `GET` | `/datasets` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 5 | `POST` | `/datasets` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 6 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 7 | `PUT` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 8 | `DELETE` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active (soft delete) |\n| 9 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}/records` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 10 | `POST` | `/datasets/{id}/records` | **bulk** | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 11 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 12 | `PATCH` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 13 | `DELETE` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active (hard delete) |\n| 14 | `POST` | `/datasets/{id}/sync` | **sync** | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 15 | `GET` | `/jobs/{job_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 16 | `GET` | `/webhooks` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 17 | `POST` | `/webhooks` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 18 | `GET` | `/webhooks/{id}` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 19 | `DELETE` | `/webhooks/{id}` | standard | v2.2.0 | active |\n| 20 | `GET` | `/me` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 21 | `PATCH` | `/me` | standard | v2.0.0 | active |\n| 22 | `GET` | `/me/api-keys` | standard | v2.0.0 | **DEPRECATED (v2.1)** |\n| 23 | `POST` | `/me/api-keys` | standard | v2.0.0 | **DEPRECATED (v2.1)** |\n| 24 | `GET` | `/me/usage` | standard | v2.1.0 | active |\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Authentication\n\n#### Authenticate and obtain tokens\n\n
\n POST /auth/login (authenticate user and get tokens — public)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------|\n> | `email` | required | string | Account email |\n> | `password` | required | string | Account password |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|--------------------------------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Tokens returned (`access_token`, `refresh_token`) |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid credentials |\n> | `429` | `application/json` | Too many attempts — back off and retry later |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -d '{\"email\":\"you@example.com\",\"password\":\"secret\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/login\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Refresh an access token\n\n
\n POST /auth/refresh (exchange a refresh token for new tokens — public)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|------------------------|\n> | `refresh_token` | required | string | Current refresh token |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|-----------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | New tokens issued |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid token |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Expired token — log in again |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -d '{\"refresh_token\":\"d9f0c1...\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/refresh\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Invalidate tokens\n\n
\n POST /auth/logout (invalidate tokens — requires auth)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-----------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|\n> | `refresh_token` | optional | string | Specific token to invalidate; if omitted, **all** tokens for the user are invalidated |\n\n*(Request body — JSON, optional)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"refresh_token\":\"d9f0c1...\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/logout\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Datasets\n\n#### List datasets\n\n
\n GET /datasets (list all datasets for the authenticated user)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------|\n> | `page` | optional | int | Page number (default `1`) |\n> | `limit` | optional | int | Items per page (default `20`, max `100`) |\n> | `status` | optional | string | Filter: `active` \\| `archived` \\| `all` (default `all`) |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|---------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset list |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> \"https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets?page=1&limit=20&status=active\"\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Create a dataset\n\n
\n POST /datasets (create a new dataset)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------|\n> | `name` | required | string | Dataset name — must be 3–100 characters and unique |\n> | `description` | optional | string | Human-readable description |\n> | `tags` | optional | array | List of tags |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `409` | `application/json` | Duplicate name |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"name\":\"Quarterly metrics\",\"description\":\"Q4 data\",\"tags\":[\"finance\"]}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Get a dataset\n\n
\n GET /datasets/{id} (get a single dataset by ID)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID |\n\nReturns `404` if the dataset does not exist or is not owned by the authenticated user.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|-------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Update a dataset\n\n
\n PUT /datasets/{id} (update a dataset)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `name` | optional | string | New name (3–100 chars, unique) |\n> | `description` | optional | string | New description |\n> | `tags` | optional | array | New tag list |\n\n*(Request body — JSON; same fields as create, all optional)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X PUT -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"description\":\"Updated description\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Archive (soft-delete) a dataset\n\n
\n DELETE /datasets/{id} (archive a dataset — soft delete)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------|-----------|-----------|----------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID |\n\n> **This is a soft delete.** The dataset's archived flag is set; it is not permanently removed and remains retrievable via `GET /datasets?status=archived`. Archiving emits a **`dataset.updated`** webhook event — there is no `dataset.deleted` event.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X DELETE -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### List records in a dataset\n\n
\n GET /datasets/{id}/records (list records in a dataset)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `page` | optional | int | Page number (default `1`) |\n> | `limit` | optional | int | Items per page (default `20`, max `100`) |\n> | `sort` | optional | string | Field name to sort by |\n> | `order` | optional | string | `asc` (default) \\| `desc` |\n> | `filter` | optional | string | JSON-encoded filter query |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|----------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Record list |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> \"https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records?page=1&limit=20&sort=created_at&order=desc&filter=%7B%22status%22%3A%22active%22%7D\"\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Add records to a dataset (bulk-capable)\n\n
\n POST /datasets/{id}/records (add records — single object or array, max 1,000 per request)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-----------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `records` | required | array | Records to add; a single record object is also accepted. **Max 1,000 records per request.** |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n> **Rate limit category: `bulk`.** This endpoint is counted against the bulk rate limit category, which is separate from (and lower than) the standard budget — e.g., 20 requests/minute on the Free tier. Batch records up to the 1,000-per-request maximum.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|----------------------|\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"records\":[{\"field1\":\"a\"},{\"field1\":\"b\"}]}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Get a single record\n\n
\n GET /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (get a single record)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID |\n> | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Record |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Update a single record\n\n
\n PATCH /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (partial update of a single record)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID (path) |\n> | *field:value pairs* | required | object | Partial record object — only the fields to change |\n\n*(Request body — JSON; partial update only)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X PATCH -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"status\":\"reviewed\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Delete a single record\n\n
\n DELETE /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (delete a single record — hard delete)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID |\n> | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID |\n\n> Unlike dataset deletion (archive/soft delete), **record deletion is a hard delete** and cannot be undone.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X DELETE -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Trigger a sync\n\n
\n POST /datasets/{id}/sync (trigger an async sync job with an external source)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |-------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) |\n> | `source_id` | required | string | External source identifier |\n> | `mode` | optional | string | `full` (default) \\| `incremental` — incremental transfers only changes since the last successful sync |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n> The call is asynchronous: a `202` response means the job was accepted; track it via `GET /jobs/{job_id}` or the `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhook events.\n>\n> **Rate limit category: `sync`.** Sync requests are counted in their own category, separate from the standard budget.\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|--------------------|\n> | `202` | `application/json` | Job started (returns job identifier) |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid source |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"source_id\":\"src_123\",\"mode\":\"incremental\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/sync\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Jobs\n\n#### Check async job status\n\n
\n GET /jobs/{job_id} (check the status of an async job, e.g. a sync)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|-------------|\n> | `job_id` | required | string | Job identifier returned by the operation that started it |\n\n##### Response payload\n\n`data` contains: `status` (`pending` | `running` | `completed` | `failed`), `progress` (0–100), `error` (string or `null`).\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Job status |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Job not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/jobs/job_789\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Webhooks\n\nWebhook subscriptions push notifications to your HTTPS endpoint when events occur. Supported events:\n\n| Event | Fired when |\n|---|---|\n| `dataset.created` | A dataset is created |\n| `dataset.updated` | A dataset is updated **or archived** (soft delete) |\n| `sync.completed` | A sync job completes successfully |\n| `sync.failed` | A sync job fails |\n\n> **There is no `dataset.deleted` event.** `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a soft delete (archive) that emits `dataset.updated`.\n\nPayload shape for every delivery:\n\n```json\n{\n \"event\": \"dataset.updated\",\n \"timestamp\": \"ISO8601\",\n \"data\": { \"...\" : \"event-specific fields\" }\n}\n```\n\n#### List webhooks\n\n
\n GET /webhooks (list configured webhooks)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> None\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|--------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook list |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Create a webhook\n\n
\n POST /webhooks (create a webhook subscription)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n> | `url` | required | string | HTTPS endpoint that will receive deliveries |\n> | `events` | required | array | Events to subscribe to: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed` |\n> | `secret` | optional | string | Signing secret — when set, deliveries include an `X-Webhook-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body) |\n\n*(Request body — JSON)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `201` | `application/json` | Created |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"url\":\"https://hooks.example.com/datasync\",\"events\":[\"dataset.created\",\"dataset.updated\",\"sync.completed\",\"sync.failed\"],\"secret\":\"whsec_...\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Get webhook details\n\n
\n GET /webhooks/{id} (get webhook details)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------|-----------|-----------|-------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Webhook ID |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks/wh_001\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Delete a webhook\n\n
\n DELETE /webhooks/{id} (remove a webhook subscription)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------|-----------|-----------|-------------|\n> | `id` | required | string | Webhook ID |\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------|\n> | `204` | None | Success |\n> | `404` | `application/json` | Not found |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X DELETE -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks/wh_001\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n### Webhook signature verification\n\nWhen a webhook is created **with a `secret`**, every delivery includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header containing the **HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body**, keyed with that secret. Verify it before processing any delivery:\n\n1. **Read the raw request body** — the exact bytes as received. Do *not* re-serialize a parsed JSON object; key ordering and whitespace differences will change the signature.\n2. **Compute the expected signature** — HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body using your webhook secret as the key.\n3. **Compare in constant time** — use a timing-safe comparison (e.g., `hmac.compare_digest` in Python). Never compare with `==`.\n4. **Reject mismatches** — return an error status (e.g., `400`) and do not process the payload.\n\nReference implementation (Python):\n\n```python\nimport hmac, hashlib\n\ndef verify_webhook(request_body: bytes, received_signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:\n expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), request_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()\n return hmac.compare_digest(expected, received_signature)\n\n# In your handler:\n# sig = request.headers.get(\"X-Webhook-Signature\")\n# if not verify_webhook(request.get_data(), sig, WEBHOOK_SECRET):\n# abort(400)\n```\n\nCommon verification failures:\n\n| Symptom | Cause |\n|---|---|\n| Every signature check fails | Verifying against the parsed/re-serialized JSON instead of the raw body |\n| Signature valid locally, missing at the receiver | A proxy or framework consumed the body before your handler read the raw bytes |\n| Intermittent failures after rotation | An old webhook (old secret) still active alongside the new one — delete the stale subscription |\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n## Account\n\n#### Get current user profile\n\n
\n GET /me (get the current user profile)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> None\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|-------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | User profile |\n> | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/me\n> ```\n\n
\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#### Update current user profile\n\n
\n PATCH /me (update the current user profile)\n\n##### Parameters\n\n> | name | type | data type | description |\n> |------------|-----------|-----------|---------------|\n> | `name` | optional | string | Display name |\n> | `email` | optional | string | Email address |\n> | `timezone` | optional | string | Timezone |\n\n*(Request body — JSON; partial update)*\n\n##### Responses\n\n> | http code | content-type | response |\n> |-----------|------------------|------------------|\n> | `200` | `application/json` | Updated |\n> | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error |\n\n##### Example cURL\n\n> ```javascript\n> curl -X PATCH -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n> -H \"Authorization: Bearer \" \\\n> -d '{\"timezone\":\"Europe/Berlin\"}' \\\n> https://api.datasync.io/v2/me\n> ```\n\n

Authentication error diagnostics\n\n### 1.1 `401 Unauthorized` — decision tree\n\nWork down the list in order:\n\n1. **Is the `Authorization` header present and well-formed?**\n   Correct format: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.\n   - Missing header → `401`.\n   - Wrong scheme (e.g., sending the token without the `Bearer` prefix, or a legacy API key credential in a bearer-style header) → `401`. If your process caches a token across long runs, refresh it (`POST /auth/refresh`) proactively — don't wait for the 401.\n3. **Was the token invalidated?** `POST /auth/logout` invalidates tokens — and if called **without** a `refresh_token` in the body, it invalidates **all** tokens for the user. If another team member or job ran a full logout, every outstanding token stops working. Re-login.\n4. **Is the refresh token the problem?** Distinguish the two refresh failures:\n   - `400` from `POST /auth/refresh` → the refresh token is **invalid** — re-login with credentials.\n   - `401` from `POST /auth/refresh` → the refresh token has **expired** (they last **7 days**) — re-login with credentials.\n5. **Still authenticating with a legacy API key?** Keys remain functional during the deprecation window (removal planned for v3), but they are deprecated. Plan the JWT migration regardless — see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`.\n\n### 1.2 `401` vs `403` — which one means what\n\n| Code | Meaning | Typical fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| `401` | Not authenticated — the server cannot verify who you are | Fix the token (sections 1.1) |\n| `403` | Forbidden — authenticated, but not authorized for this resource | Use credentials/resource your user actually owns |\n\n**Known behavior:** in some cases an authorization failure (valid token, insufficient permissions) is reported as `401` instead of `403`. Back off and retry later; do not loop login attempts in a retry storm. Batch services behind a shared token service so 40+ processes are not each performing logins.\n\n### 1.4 Auth error quick reference\n\n| Where | Response | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Any endpoint | `401` | Not authenticated / token expired / token invalidated | Check header, refresh or re-login |\n| Any endpoint | `403` | Authenticated but not authorized | Check resource ownership/permissions |\n| `POST /auth/login` | `400` | Invalid credentials | Check email/password |\n| `POST /auth/login` | `429` | Too many attempts | Back off; centralize token acquisition |\n| `POST /auth/refresh` | `400` | Invalid refresh token | Re-login |\n| `POST /auth/refresh` | `401` | Refresh token expired (7 days) | Re-login |\n\n---\n\n## 2. Rate limiting\n\n### 2.1 Categories — the part most integrations miss\n\nRate limits are enforced **per category**, not only per plan. Every endpoint belongs to exactly one category:\n\n| Category | Endpoints counted | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `standard` | All endpoints **except** the two below (22 of 24 operations) | The default budget |\n| `bulk` | `POST /datasets/{id}/records` only | Separate budget, **lower** than standard |\n| `sync` | `POST /datasets/{id}/sync` only | Separate budget, independent of standard |\n\nSo on the Free tier, 60 standard `GET` requests plus 25 bulk inserts in the same minute does **not** fit: the 60 are fine, the 25 bulk requests exceed the 20/min bulk budget and the 21st onward get `429` — even though you are far under 100 req/min overall.\n\n### 2.2 Limits by tier\n\n| Tier | Standard | Bulk | Sync | Daily cap |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Free | 100 req/min | **20 req/min** | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | 10,000 req/day |\n| Pro | 1,000 req/min | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Separate budget — current value returned in `X-RateLimit-Limit` | None |\n| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom |\n\nThe authoritative limit for your plan and category is always exposed in the `X-RateLimit-Limit` response header — read it once from a live call rather than hardcoding assumptions.\n\n### 2.3 Rate limit response headers\n\nEvery response (success or `429`) carries:\n\n| Header | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Maximum requests per window for that category |\n| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests remaining in the current window |\n| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp when the window resets |\n\n> Headers on `429` responses have been reliable since v2.1 (a v2.0 defect omitted them). Webhook issues\n\n### 3.1 Not receiving callbacks — checklist\n\n1. **List your actual subscriptions** with `GET /webhooks` and compare the `events` array to what you expect.\n2. **Are you subscribed to an event that doesn't exist?** The valid events are exactly: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed`. Common migration pitfalls (v2.0 → v2.2)\n\nCompiled from recurring support patterns. Each row states the mistake, the observable symptom, and the correct behavior.\n\n| # | Pitfall | Symptom | Correct behavior |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Assuming old auth still works unchanged | `401` after upgrade | JWT is the standard since v2.1; API keys are deprecated but still work during the window — verify header format first (`MIGRATION_GUIDE` §3) |\n| 2 | Caching access tokens beyond their ~1 h lifetime | Sudden `401`s after an hour of operation | Refresh proactively or retry once on 401 after refreshing |\n| 3 | Subscribing to `dataset.deleted` | No callbacks when datasets are archived | Event doesn't exist; `DELETE /datasets/{id}` is a soft delete that emits `dataset.updated` |\n| 4 | Treating dataset deletion as permanent | Dataset \"gone\" but still in storage | Soft delete sets the archived flag; retrieve with `GET /datasets?status=archived`. Track via `GET /jobs/{job_id}` or `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhooks |\n| 15 | Missing rate limit headers on 429s (v2.0 behavior) | Retry logic without backoff timing | Fixed in v2.1 — headers are present on all responses, including `429` |\n| 16 | Ignoring `422` | Confusing business-rule failures with validation bugs | `400` = field validation (see `errors` array); `422` = business rule violation |\n| 17 | Retrying `500` immediately and repeatedly | Extended disruption | Back off; include `meta.request_id` in the support ticket |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Escalated scenario walkthroughs\n\nThe three Customer Success escalations that triggered this documentation, anonymized, with the resolution paths.\n\n### Scenario A — \"JWT migration breaking our integration\" (Enterprise, dozens of microservices)\n\n- **Symptom:** `401` errors after upgrading; API keys still visible in the dashboard; legacy key endpoints still return 200; no published transition guidance.\n- **Diagnosis:** v2.1 switched to JWT and deprecated API keys. Keys remain valid during the deprecation window (removal in v3), and parallel authentication is supported — so a working integration can move service by service.\n- **Resolution:** staged migration — keep keys for un-migrated services, stand up a shared token service for JWT issuance/refresh, migrate waves of services, retire the key when the last wave completes. Decision criteria and before/after code: `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md` §3.\n- **Prevention:** never create new API keys; treat `GET`/`POST /me/api-keys` as transition-only.\n\n### Scenario B — \"Webhook not firing for deleted datasets\" (Pro tier)\n\n- **Symptom:** webhook subscribed to five event names; callbacks received for `created`/`updated` but never for `dataset.deleted`.\n- **Diagnosis:** `dataset.deleted` is not an implemented event. `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a soft delete (archive) that triggers `dataset.updated`.\n- **Resolution:** remove `dataset.deleted` from the subscription; subscribe to `dataset.updated` and branch on the archived flag in the payload (`MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md` §5.3). Error code reference\n\n| HTTP code | Meaning | What to do |\n|---|---|---|\n| `400` | Bad request — validation failed | Read the field-level `errors` array in the body; fix the payload. 1: # Developer Notes - DataSync API
2: # These are internal notes from the dev team - NOT for external publication
3: # Last updated by multiple contributors
4: 
5: == AUTH STUFF ==
6: We use JWT tokens now. Changed from API keys last sprint (v2.1).
7: Token expires in 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
8: Header format: Authorization: Bearer <token>
9: Login endpoint: POST /auth/login - takes email+password, returns tokens
10: Refresh: POST /auth/refresh - takes refresh_token in body
11: 
12: BUG: Sometimes 401 returns instead of 403 when token valid but perms wrong
13: TODO: Fix in next sprint (JIRA-4521)
14: 
15: == DATA ENDPOINTS ==
16: 
17: /datasets - GET list all datasets for user
18: params: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100), status (active|archived|all)
19: returns array of dataset objects
20: 
21: /datasets/{id} - GET single dataset
22: 404 if not found or not owned by user
23: 
24: /datasets - POST create new dataset
25: body: { name: string (required, 3-100 chars), description: string (optional), tags: array }
26: returns created dataset with id
27: 
28: /datasets/{id} - PUT update dataset
29: same body as POST but all fields optional
30: returns updated dataset
31: 
32: /datasets/{id} - DELETE soft delete (sets archived flag)
33: returns 204 no content
34: 
35: /datasets/{id}/records - GET records in dataset
36: pagination same as /datasets list
37: params: sort (field name), order (asc|desc), filter (JSON encoded query)
38: 
39: /datasets/{id}/records - POST add record(s)
40: body can be single object or array for bulk insert
41: max 1000 records per request
42: 
43: /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} - PATCH update single record
44: body: partial record object
45: 
46: /datasets/{id}/sync - POST trigger sync with external source
47: body: { source_id: string, mode: "full"|"incremental" }
48: returns job_id for async tracking
49: 
50: /jobs/{job_id} - GET check job status
51: response: { status: "pending"|"running"|"completed"|"failed", progress: 0-100, error: string|null }
52: 
53: == ERROR CODES ==
54: 
55: 400 - bad request (validation failed) - body has "errors" array with field-specific messages
56: 401 - not authenticated
57: 403 - forbidden (authenticated but not authorized)
58: 404 - not found
59: 409 - conflict (e.g., duplicate name)
60: 422 - unprocessable entity (business rule violation)
61: 429 - rate limited (100 req/min for free tier, 1000 for pro)
62: 500 - server error (we log these, include request_id in response for support)
63: 
64: == RESPONSE FORMAT ==
65: 
66: All responses wrapped:
67: {
68:   "success": true|false,
69:   "data": <payload>|null,
70:   "error": null|{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} },
71:   "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" }
72: }
73: 
74: == WEBHOOKS (v2.2 feature) ==
75: 
76: POST /webhooks - create webhook
77: body: { url: string, events: ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"], secret: string (optional, for HMAC signing) }
78: 
79: GET /webhooks - list webhooks
80: DELETE /webhooks/{id} - remove webhook
81: 
82: Webhook payload:
83: {
84:   "event": "event.type",
85:   "timestamp": "ISO8601",
86:   "data": { <event specific> }
87: }
88: 
89: If secret provided, we send X-Webhook-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 of body
90: 
91: == RATE LIMITS ==
92: 
93: Free tier: 100 requests/minute, 10000/day
94: Pro tier: 1000 requests/minute, unlimited daily
95: Enterprise: custom
96: 
97: Headers returned:
98: X-RateLimit-Limit: <max>
99: X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining>
100: X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix timestamp>
101: 
102: == SDK notes ==
103: 
104: Python SDK wraps all this, handles auth refresh automatically
105: JS SDK in beta - dont document yet
106: Java SDK abandoned - dont mention
107: 
108: == CHANGELOG snippets ==
109: 
110: v2.2.0 (2024-12-15)
111: - Added webhooks
112: - Fixed: sync jobs sometimes stuck in "running"
113: - Improved: bulk insert now 3x faster
114: 
115: v2.1.0 (2024-11-01)
116: - BREAKING: Switched to JWT auth (API keys deprecated, removed in v3)
117: - Added incremental sync mode
118: - Fixed: rate limit headers missing on 429 responses
119: 
120: v2.0.0 (2024-09-15)
121: - Complete rewrite
122: - New endpoint structure
123: - Added job queue for async operations
124: 
125: == MISC ==
126: 
127: Base URL: https://api.datasync.io/v2
128: Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2 (resets daily, fake data ok)
129: 
130: Content-Type must be application/json for all POST/PUT/PATCH
131: 
132: CORS enabled for *.datasync.io domains, customers can request whitelist
133: 
134: OpenAPI spec is auto-generated but has bugs - dont use directly, needs manual cleanup

(End of file - total 134 lines)

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Normalize a delimited data file (CSV/TSV) whose cells may contain
3: inner-delimited multi-value fields, and report the counts needed to
4: reconcile a deliverable against its source.
5: 
6: Usage:
7:   python3 scripts/normalize_delimited.py <file.csv> [--delimiter ,] [--inner ;]
8:       [--fields col1,col2] [--out out.json] [--markdown] [--max-col-width 40]
9: 
10: Behavior:
11:   * Parses with the csv module (quoted fields handled correctly).
12:   * If --inner is given, every cell (or only --fields columns) that contains
13:     the inner delimiter is split into a list; a cell without it stays as-is.
14:   * Prints: row count, column list, per-column non-empty counts, per-column
15:     count of cells containing the inner delimiter, and duplicate-key check on
16:     the first column if --key is given.
17:   * With --out, writes a JSON array of row objects (inner-split values as lists).
18:   * With --markdown, prints a markdown table of the normalized rows.
19: 
20: Exit code 0 on success; row/cell counts are printed on stdout for reuse.
21: """
22: 
23: import argparse
24: import csv
25: import json
26: import sys
27: 
28: 
29: def main():
30:     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Normalize delimited data with inner multi-value cells.")
31:     ap.add_argument("path", nargs="?", default="-", help="input file, '-' for stdin")
32:     ap.add_argument("--delimiter", default=",", help="field delimiter (default ',')")
33:     ap.add_argument("--inner", default=None, help="inner delimiter for multi-value cells, e.g. ';'")
34:     ap.add_argument("--fields", default=None, help="comma-separated column names to inner-split (default: any)")
35:     ap.add_argument("--key", default=None, help="column to check for duplicate values")
36:     ap.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="write normalized rows as JSON to this path")
37:     ap.add_argument("--markdown", action="store_true", help="also print a markdown table")
38:     ap.add_argument("--max-col-width", type=int, default=40, help="markdown cell truncation width")
39:     args = ap.parse_args()
40: 
41:     handle = sys.stdin if args.path == "-" else open(args.path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig")
42:     try:
43:         reader = csv.DictReader(handle, delimiter=args.delimiter)
44:         rows = [dict(r) for r in reader]
45:         columns = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
46:     finally:
47:         if handle is not sys.stdin:
48:             handle.close()
49: 
50:     if not rows:
51:         print("ROW_COUNT 0")
52:         print("WARNING: no data rows parsed - check the delimiter")
53:         return 1
54: 
55:     split_fields = set(args.fields.split(",")) if args.fields else None
56:     inner_counts = {c: 0 for c in columns}
57:     normalized = []
58:     for row in rows:
59:         out = {}
60:         for col in columns:
61:             val = (row.get(col) or "").strip()
62:             if args.inner and val and args.inner in val and (split_fields is None or col in split_fields):
63:                 inner_counts[col] += 1
64:                 out[col] = [part.strip() for part in val.split(args.inner) if part.strip() != ""]
65:             else:
66:                 out[col] = val
67:         normalized.append(out)
68: 
69:     print("ROW_COUNT", len(normalized))
70:     print("COLUMNS", "|".join(columns))
71:     for col in columns:
72:         nonempty = sum(1 for r in normalized if r[col])
73:         print("FILLED\t%s\t%d/%d" % (col, nonempty, len(normalized)))
74:     if args.inner:
75:         for col, n in inner_counts.items():
76:             if n:
77:                 print("INNER_SPLIT\t%s\t%d" % (col, n))
78:     if args.key:
79:         if args.key not in columns:
80:             print("WARNING: key column %r not found" % args.key)
81:         else:
82:             seen, dupes = set(), []
83:             for r in normalized:
84:                 k = r[args.key]
85:                 ident = tuple(k) if isinstance(k, list) else (k,)
86:                 if ident in seen:
87:                     dupes.append(str(ident))
88:                 seen.add(ident)
89:             print("DUPLICATE_KEYS", len(dupes), "; ".join(dupes[:5]))
90: 
91:     if args.out:
92:         with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
93:             json.dump(normalized, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
94:         print("WROTE_JSON", args.out)
95: 
96:     if args.markdown:
97:         def cell(v):
98:             text = "; ".join(v) if isinstance(v, list) else str(v)
99:             text = text.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ")
100:             if len(text) > args.max_col_width:
101:                 text = text[: args.max_col_width - 1] + "\u2026"
102:             return text
103: 
104:         print("| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |")
105:         print("|" + "|".join(["---"] * len(columns)) + "|")
106:         for r in normalized:
107:             print("| " + " | ".join(cell(r[c]) for c in columns) + " |")
108:     return 0
109: 
110: 
111: if __name__ == "__main__":
112:     sys.exit(main())

v2.2.0 (2024-12-15): Webhooks (4 event types + HMAC signatures), sync jobs stuck fix, bulk insert 3x faster.

### 3.4 Decision criteria for the deprecation period
Table: factor → migrate now / can defer.
- Number of services: few → now; many (e.g., dozens of microservices) → phased, per-service rollout using parallel auth.
- Ability to store/handle refresh: yes → now; no token storage infra → plan before v3.
- Security requirements: short-lived credentials reduce exposure → earlier is better; keys are long-lived.
- New development: always JWT; do not create new API keys (POST /me/api-keys deprecated).
- Hard deadline: v3 removal — all services must be off keys before v3.
Guidance: because parallel support exists, a staged rollout is safe: keep keys for services not yet migrated, add JWT per service, flip off keys when last service done. # Troubleshooting Guide (v2.2)
## Before you start: collect diagnostics (request_id from meta; envelope)
## Authentication errors
- 401 diagnosis flow (missing/malformed header, expired access token 1h, refresh expired 7d, wrong audience...)

  1) No/invalid Authorization header → 401.
  2) Expired access token → 401 → refresh.
  3) Refresh token invalid → 400; expired → 401 (per CSV).
  4) Logged out (tokens invalidated via /auth/logout) → 401 → re-login.
  5) Known behavior: permission failures occasionally returned as 401 instead of 403 — validate token first; if valid and still denied, contact support with request_id.
- API-key era errors: if you still authenticate with legacy API keys and see 401, verify key is active; keys deprecated (removal v3); /me/api-keys still lists them.
- 403: authenticated but not authorized.
- 429 on /auth/login: too many attempts.
## Rate limiting
- Categories & mapping table; tier table; headers; 429 handling + retry strategy; free tier daily cap 10,000; login attempts 429.

{"content": "# DataSync API Reference — v2.2 REST API documentation for DataSync API v2.2, organized by resource. Formatting follows the Swagger-inspired Markdown style (collapsible endpoint sections, parameter tables, response tables, cURL examples). **Base URL:** `https://api.datasync.io/v2` **Sandbox:** `https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2` (resets daily) --- ## Conventions ### Authentication All endpoints require authentication unless marked *public*. Send a JWT access token in the `Authorization` header: ``` Authorization: Bearer ``` Obtain tokens via `POST /auth/login`; refresh via `POST /auth/refresh`. Access tokens live ~1 hour, refresh tokens 7 days. Legacy API key authentication is **deprecated** (removal planned for v3) — see `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`. ### Request format `Content-Type: application/json` is required for all `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` requests. ### Response envelope Every response is wrapped in a standard envelope: ```json { "success": true, "data": {}, "error": null, "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" } } ``` On failure, `success` is `false`, `data` is `null`, and `error` is an object: `{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} }`. Validation failures (`400`) include a field-level `errors` array. Server errors (`500`) include a `request_id` in `meta` — include it when contacting support. ### Error codes | HTTP code | Meaning | |---|---| | `400` | Bad request — validation failed; body contains field-specific messages | | `401` | Not authenticated | | `403` | Forbidden — authenticated but not authorized | | `404` | Not found | | `409` | Conflict (e.g., duplicate dataset name) | | `422` | Unprocessable entity — business rule violation | | `429` | Rate limited | | `500` | Server error | ### Rate limits Requests are counted in three categories: **standard**, **bulk**, and **sync**. Every response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix timestamp) headers; on `429`, wait until the reset time before retrying. See `TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md` for the full per-tier matrix. ### Pagination List endpoints accept `page` (default `1`) and `limit` (default `20`, maximum `100`). --- ## Endpoint inventory | # | Method | Endpoint | Rate category | Added | Status | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `POST` | `/auth/login` | standard | v2.1.0 | active (public) | | 2 | `POST` | `/auth/refresh` | standard | v2.1.0 | active (public) | | 3 | `POST` | `/auth/logout` | standard | v2.1.0 | active | | 4 | `GET` | `/datasets` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 5 | `POST` | `/datasets` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 6 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 7 | `PUT` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 8 | `DELETE` | `/datasets/{id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active (soft delete) | | 9 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}/records` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 10 | `POST` | `/datasets/{id}/records` | **bulk** | v2.0.0 | active | | 11 | `GET` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 12 | `PATCH` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 13 | `DELETE` | `/datasets/{id}/records/{record_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active (hard delete) | | 14 | `POST` | `/datasets/{id}/sync` | **sync** | v2.0.0 | active | | 15 | `GET` | `/jobs/{job_id}` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 16 | `GET` | `/webhooks` | standard | v2.2.0 | active | | 17 | `POST` | `/webhooks` | standard | v2.2.0 | active | | 18 | `GET` | `/webhooks/{id}` | standard | v2.2.0 | active | | 19 | `DELETE` | `/webhooks/{id}` | standard | v2.2.0 | active | | 20 | `GET` | `/me` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 21 | `PATCH` | `/me` | standard | v2.0.0 | active | | 22 | `GET` | `/me/api-keys` | standard | v2.0.0 | **DEPRECATED (v2.1)** | | 23 | `POST` | `/me/api-keys` | standard | v2.0.0 | **DEPRECATED (v2.1)** | | 24 | `GET` | `/me/usage` | standard | v2.1.0 | active | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Authentication #### Authenticate and obtain tokens
POST /auth/login (authenticate user and get tokens — public) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------| > | `email` | required | string | Account email | > | `password` | required | string | Account password | *(Request body — JSON)* ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|--------------------------------------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Tokens returned (`access_token`, `refresh_token`) | > | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid credentials | > | `429` | `application/json` | Too many attempts — back off and retry later | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -d '{"email":"you@example.com","password":"secret"}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/login > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Refresh an access token
POST /auth/refresh (exchange a refresh token for new tokens — public) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |-----------------|-----------|-----------|------------------------| > | `refresh_token` | required | string | Current refresh token | *(Request body — JSON)* ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|-----------------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | New tokens issued | > | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid token | > | `401` | `application/json` | Expired token — log in again | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -d '{"refresh_token":"d9f0c1..."}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/refresh > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Invalidate tokens
POST /auth/logout (invalidate tokens — requires auth) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |-----------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------| > | `refresh_token` | optional | string | Specific token to invalidate; if omitted, **all** tokens for the user are invalidated | *(Request body — JSON, optional)* ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------| > | `204` | None | Success | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -d '{"refresh_token":"d9f0c1..."}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/auth/logout > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Datasets #### List datasets
GET /datasets (list all datasets for the authenticated user) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------| > | `page` | optional | int | Page number (default `1`) | > | `limit` | optional | int | Items per page (default `20`, max `100`) | > | `status` | optional | string | Filter: `active` \| `archived` \| `all` (default `all`) | ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|---------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset list | > | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > "https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets?page=1&limit=20&status=active" > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Create a dataset
POST /datasets (create a new dataset) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------| > | `name` | required | string | Dataset name — must be 3–100 characters and unique | > | `description` | optional | string | Human-readable description | > | `tags` | optional | array | List of tags | *(Request body — JSON)* ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------------| > | `201` | `application/json` | Created | > | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error | > | `409` | `application/json` | Duplicate name | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -d '{"name":"Quarterly metrics","description":"Q4 data","tags":["finance"]}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Get a dataset
GET /datasets/{id} (get a single dataset by ID) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |------|-----------|-----------|-----------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID | Returns `404` if the dataset does not exist or is not owned by the authenticated user. ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|-------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Dataset | > | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized | > | `404` | `application/json` | Not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Update a dataset
PUT /datasets/{id} (update a dataset) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |---------------|-----------|-----------|--------------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) | > | `name` | optional | string | New name (3–100 chars, unique) | > | `description` | optional | string | New description | > | `tags` | optional | array | New tag list | *(Request body — JSON; same fields as create, all optional)* ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Updated | > | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error | > | `404` | `application/json` | Not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -d '{"description":"Updated description"}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Archive (soft-delete) a dataset
DELETE /datasets/{id} (archive a dataset — soft delete) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |------|-----------|-----------|----------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID | > **This is a soft delete.** The dataset's archived flag is set; it is not permanently removed and remains retrievable via `GET /datasets?status=archived`. Archiving emits a **`dataset.updated`** webhook event — there is no `dataset.deleted` event. ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------| > | `204` | None | Success | > | `404` | `application/json` | Not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### List records in a dataset
GET /datasets/{id}/records (list records in a dataset) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |----------|-----------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) | > | `page` | optional | int | Page number (default `1`) | > | `limit` | optional | int | Items per page (default `20`, max `100`) | > | `sort` | optional | string | Field name to sort by | > | `order` | optional | string | `asc` (default) \| `desc` | > | `filter` | optional | string | JSON-encoded filter query | ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|----------------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Record list | > | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > "https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records?page=1&limit=20&sort=created_at&order=desc&filter=%7B%22status%22%3A%22active%22%7D" > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Add records to a dataset (bulk-capable)
POST /datasets/{id}/records (add records — single object or array, max 1,000 per request) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |-----------|-----------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) | > | `records` | required | array | Records to add; a single record object is also accepted. **Max 1,000 records per request.** | *(Request body — JSON)* > **Rate limit category: `bulk`.** This endpoint is counted against the bulk rate limit category, which is separate from (and lower than) the standard budget — e.g., 20 requests/minute on the Free tier. Batch records up to the 1,000-per-request maximum. ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|----------------------| > | `201` | `application/json` | Created | > | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error | > | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -d '{"records":[{"field1":"a"},{"field1":"b"}]}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Get a single record
GET /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (get a single record) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID | > | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID | ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Record | > | `404` | `application/json` | Not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Update a single record
PATCH /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (partial update of a single record) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------------------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) | > | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID (path) | > | *field:value pairs* | required | object | Partial record object — only the fields to change | *(Request body — JSON; partial update only)* ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Updated | > | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error | > | `404` | `application/json` | Not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X PATCH -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -d '{"status":"reviewed"}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Delete a single record
DELETE /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} (delete a single record — hard delete) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |-------------|-----------|-----------|---------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID | > | `record_id` | required | string | Record ID | > Unlike dataset deletion (archive/soft delete), **record deletion is a hard delete** and cannot be undone. ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------| > | `204` | None | Success | > | `404` | `application/json` | Not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/records/rec_456 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Trigger a sync
POST /datasets/{id}/sync (trigger an async sync job with an external source) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |-------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------| > | `id` | required | string | Dataset ID (path) | > | `source_id` | required | string | External source identifier | > | `mode` | optional | string | `full` (default) \| `incremental` — incremental transfers only changes since the last successful sync | *(Request body — JSON)* > The call is asynchronous: a `202` response means the job was accepted; track it via `GET /jobs/{job_id}` or the `sync.completed` / `sync.failed` webhook events. > > **Rate limit category: `sync`.** Sync requests are counted in their own category, separate from the standard budget. ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|--------------------| > | `202` | `application/json` | Job started (returns job identifier) | > | `400` | `application/json` | Invalid source | > | `404` | `application/json` | Dataset not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -d '{"source_id":"src_123","mode":"incremental"}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/datasets/ds_123/sync > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Jobs #### Check async job status
GET /jobs/{job_id} (check the status of an async job, e.g. a sync) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |----------|-----------|-----------|-------------| > | `job_id` | required | string | Job identifier returned by the operation that started it | ##### Response payload `data` contains: `status` (`pending` | `running` | `completed` | `failed`), `progress` (0–100), `error` (string or `null`). ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Job status | > | `404` | `application/json` | Job not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/jobs/job_789 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Webhooks Webhook subscriptions push notifications to your HTTPS endpoint when events occur. Supported events: | Event | Fired when | |---|---| | `dataset.created` | A dataset is created | | `dataset.updated` | A dataset is updated **or archived** (soft delete) | | `sync.completed` | A sync job completes successfully | | `sync.failed` | A sync job fails | > **There is no `dataset.deleted` event.** `DELETE /datasets/{id}` performs a soft delete (archive) that emits `dataset.updated`. Payload shape for every delivery: ```json { "event": "dataset.updated", "timestamp": "ISO8601", "data": { "..." : "event-specific fields" } } ``` #### List webhooks
GET /webhooks (list configured webhooks) ##### Parameters > None ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|--------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook list | > | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Create a webhook
POST /webhooks (create a webhook subscription) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |----------|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------| > | `url` | required | string | HTTPS endpoint that will receive deliveries | > | `events` | required | array | Events to subscribe to: `dataset.created`, `dataset.updated`, `sync.completed`, `sync.failed` | > | `secret` | optional | string | Signing secret — when set, deliveries include an `X-Webhook-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body) | *(Request body — JSON)* ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------------| > | `201` | `application/json` | Created | > | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -d '{"url":"https://hooks.example.com/datasync","events":["dataset.created","dataset.updated","sync.completed","sync.failed"],"secret":"whsec_..."}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Get webhook details
GET /webhooks/{id} (get webhook details) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |------|-----------|-----------|-------------| > | `id` | required | string | Webhook ID | ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Webhook | > | `404` | `application/json` | Not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks/wh_001 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Delete a webhook
DELETE /webhooks/{id} (remove a webhook subscription) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |------|-----------|-----------|-------------| > | `id` | required | string | Webhook ID | ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------| > | `204` | None | Success | > | `404` | `application/json` | Not found | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/webhooks/wh_001 > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Webhook signature verification When a webhook is created **with a `secret`**, every delivery includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header containing the **HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body**, keyed with that secret. Verify it before processing any delivery: 1. **Read the raw request body** — the exact bytes as received. Do *not* re-serialize a parsed JSON object; key ordering and whitespace differences will change the signature. 2. **Compute the expected signature** — HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body using your webhook secret as the key. 3. **Compare in constant time** — use a timing-safe comparison (e.g., `hmac.compare_digest` in Python). Never compare with `==`. 4. **Reject mismatches** — return an error status (e.g., `400`) and do not process the payload. Reference implementation (Python): ```python import hmac, hashlib def verify_webhook(request_body: bytes, received_signature: str, secret: str) -> bool: expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), request_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() return hmac.compare_digest(expected, received_signature) # In your handler: # sig = request.headers.get("X-Webhook-Signature") # if not verify_webhook(request.get_data(), sig, WEBHOOK_SECRET): # abort(400) ``` Common verification failures: | Symptom | Cause | |---|---| | Every signature check fails | Verifying against the parsed/re-serialized JSON instead of the raw body | | Signature valid locally, missing at the receiver | A proxy or framework consumed the body before your handler read the raw bytes | | Intermittent failures after rotation | An old webhook (old secret) still active alongside the new one — delete the stale subscription | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Account #### Get current user profile
GET /me (get the current user profile) ##### Parameters > None ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|-------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | User profile | > | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/me > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Update current user profile
PATCH /me (update the current user profile) ##### Parameters > | name | type | data type | description | > |------------|-----------|-----------|---------------| > | `name` | optional | string | Display name | > | `email` | optional | string | Email address | > | `timezone` | optional | string | Timezone | *(Request body — JSON; partial update)* ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|------------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Updated | > | `400` | `application/json` | Validation error | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -X PATCH -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -d '{"timezone":"Europe/Berlin"}' \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/me > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### List API keys *(legacy)*
GET /me/api-keys (DEPRECATED — list API keys) > ![Deprecated](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-deprecated-red) **Deprecated since v2.1.** DataSync uses JWT authentication (`POST /auth/login`). API keys remain functional during the deprecation window only and will be removed in v3. See `MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md`. ##### Parameters > None ##### Responses > | http code | content-type | response | > |-----------|------------------|-------------| > | `200` | `application/json` | Key list | > | `401` | `application/json` | Unauthorized | ##### Example cURL > ```javascript > curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > https://api.datasync.io/v2/me/api-keys > ```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Create an API key *(legacy)*

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Webhook signature verification When a webhook is created **with a `secret`**, every delivery includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header containing the **HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body**, keyed with that secret. Verify it before processing any delivery: 1. **Read the raw request body** — the exact bytes as received. Do *not* re-serialize a parsed JSON object; key ordering and whitespace differences will change the signature. 2. **Compute the expected signature** — HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body using your webhook secret as the key. 3. **Compare in constant time** — use a timing-safe comparison (e.g., `hmac.compare_digest` in Python). Never compare with `==`. 4. **Reject mismatches** — return an error status (e.g., `400`) and do not process the payload. Reference implementation (Python): ```python import hmac, hashlib def verify_webhook(request_body: bytes, received_signature: str, secret: str) -> bool: expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), request_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() return hmac.compare_digest(expected, received_signature) # In your handler: # sig = request.headers.get("X-Webhook-Signature") # if not verify_webhook(request.get_data(), sig, WEBHOOK_SECRET): # abort(400) ``` Common verification failures: | Symptom | Cause | |---|---| | Every signature check fails | Verifying against the parsed/re-serialized JSON instead of the raw body | | Signature valid locally, missing at the receiver | A proxy or framework consumed the body before your handler read the raw bytes | | Intermittent failures after rotation | An old webhook (old secret) still active alongside the new one — delete the stale subscription | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Account #### Get current user profile

1: # Developer Notes - DataSync API
2: # These are internal notes from the dev team - NOT for external publication
3: # Last updated by multiple contributors
4: 
5: == AUTH STUFF ==
6: We use JWT tokens now. Changed from API keys last sprint (v2.1).
7: Token expires in 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 7 days.
8: Header format: Authorization: Bearer <token>
9: Login endpoint: POST /auth/login - takes email+password, returns tokens
10: Refresh: POST /auth/refresh - takes refresh_token in body
11: 
12: BUG: Sometimes 401 returns instead of 403 when token valid but perms wrong
13: TODO: Fix in next sprint (JIRA-4521)
14: 
15: == DATA ENDPOINTS ==
16: 
17: /datasets - GET list all datasets for user
18: params: page (default 1), limit (default 20, max 100), status (active|archived|all)
19: returns array of dataset objects
20: 
21: /datasets/{id} - GET single dataset
22: 404 if not found or not owned by user
23: 
24: /datasets - POST create new dataset
25: body: { name: string (required, 3-100 chars), description: string (optional), tags: array }
26: returns created dataset with id
27: 
28: /datasets/{id} - PUT update dataset
29: same body as POST but all fields optional
30: returns updated dataset
31: 
32: /datasets/{id} - DELETE soft delete (sets archived flag)
33: returns 204 no content
34: 
35: /datasets/{id}/records - GET records in dataset
36: pagination same as /datasets list
37: params: sort (field name), order (asc|desc), filter (JSON encoded query)
38: 
39: /datasets/{id}/records - POST add record(s)
40: body can be single object or array for bulk insert
41: max 1000 records per request
42: 
43: /datasets/{id}/records/{record_id} - PATCH update single record
44: body: partial record object
45: 
46: /datasets/{id}/sync - POST trigger sync with external source
47: body: { source_id: string, mode: "full"|"incremental" }
48: returns job_id for async tracking
49: 
50: /jobs/{job_id} - GET check job status
51: response: { status: "pending"|"running"|"completed"|"failed", progress: 0-100, error: string|null }
52: 
53: == ERROR CODES ==
54: 
55: 400 - bad request (validation failed) - body has "errors" array with field-specific messages
56: 401 - not authenticated
57: 403 - forbidden (authenticated but not authorized)
58: 404 - not found
59: 409 - conflict (e.g., duplicate name)
60: 422 - unprocessable entity (business rule violation)
61: 429 - rate limited (100 req/min for free tier, 1000 for pro)
62: 500 - server error (we log these, include request_id in response for support)
63: 
64: == RESPONSE FORMAT ==
65: 
66: All responses wrapped:
67: {
68:   "success": true|false,
69:   "data": <payload>|null,
70:   "error": null|{ "code": "ERR_CODE", "message": "Human readable", "details": {} },
71:   "meta": { "request_id": "uuid", "timestamp": "ISO8601" }
72: }
73: 
74: == WEBHOOKS (v2.2 feature) ==
75: 
76: POST /webhooks - create webhook
77: body: { url: string, events: ["dataset.created", "dataset.updated", "sync.completed", "sync.failed"], secret: string (optional, for HMAC signing) }
78: 
79: GET /webhooks - list webhooks
80: DELETE /webhooks/{id} - remove webhook
81: 
82: Webhook payload:
83: {
84:   "event": "event.type",
85:   "timestamp": "ISO8601",
86:   "data": { <event specific> }
87: }
88: 
89: If secret provided, we send X-Webhook-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 of body
90: 
91: == RATE LIMITS ==
92: 
93: Free tier: 100 requests/minute, 10000/day
94: Pro tier: 1000 requests/minute, unlimited daily
95: Enterprise: custom
96: 
97: Headers returned:
98: X-RateLimit-Limit: <max>
99: X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining>
100: X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix timestamp>
101: 
102: == SDK notes ==
103: 
104: Python SDK wraps all this, handles auth refresh automatically
105: JS SDK in beta - dont document yet
106: Java SDK abandoned - dont mention
107: 
108: == CHANGELOG snippets ==
109: 
110: v2.2.0 (2024-12-15)
111: - Added webhooks
112: - Fixed: sync jobs sometimes stuck in "running"
113: - Improved: bulk insert now 3x faster
114: 
115: v2.1.0 (2024-11-01)
116: - BREAKING: Switched to JWT auth (API keys deprecated, removed in v3)
117: - Added incremental sync mode
118: - Fixed: rate limit headers missing on 429 responses
119: 
120: v2.0.0 (2024-09-15)
121: - Complete rewrite
122: - New endpoint structure
123: - Added job queue for async operations
124: 
125: == MISC ==
126: 
127: Base URL: https://api.datasync.io/v2
128: Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.datasync.io/v2 (resets daily, fake data ok)
129: 
130: Content-Type must be application/json for all POST/PUT/PATCH
131: 
132: CORS enabled for *.datasync.io domains, customers can request whitelist
133: 
134: OpenAPI spec is auto-generated but has bugs - dont use directly, needs manual cleanup

(End of file - total 134 lines)
</content>", "type": "text"}]
